name: Reference adult body mass
notes: THE ROW HANDOVER SECTION 9 SAYS IS MISSING: 'body_mass is not a ledger row and is the largest un-modelled dimorphism'. It was a hard-coded 70.0 default on three function signatures. It is now one number in one place and the model scales to it. ASSUMED, NOT SOURCED, AND DELIBERATELY SO. 70 kg is the conventional reference adult and it is entered here as the value the code already used, so that promoting it to the ledger changes NOTHING - size_factor returns exactly 1.0 and every existing result is bit-identical. Dressing it in a citation at the same time as changing the model structure would have made two changes at once and left neither testable. THE SEXED PAIR IS THE NEXT STEP AND THE SOURCE IS ALREADY WHITELISTED. SOURCES.md admits ICRP Publication 89 (reference anatomical and physiological values) as tier A, and it carries reference adult masses by sex. That extraction is NOT done here and the numbers are NOT guessed at: per directive 1.5 a citation nobody opened is worse than an honest assumption. When it lands this row becomes a male/female pair under ADR 0014 and, because every extensive quantity in the model now scales through it, it will move the whole model for both sexes at once - which is exactly what the handover means by calling body mass the largest un-modelled dimorphism. WHAT SCALES THROUGH IT: see src/scaling.jl. Extensive quantities scale linearly, intensive ones do not. Linear-in-mass is exact for the volumes, which are already entered as mass fractions, and is an APPROXIMATION for GFR and cardiac output, which are conventionally normalised to body surface area and therefore grow sub-linearly with mass. Linear scaling OVERSTATES their population spread. Fixing that needs height, which this model does not carry. Recorded as debt rather than approximated with an unsourced allometric exponent. CLARIFIED 2026-08-27 WHEN THE NHANES EXTRACTION LANDED. This row is the mass at which this ledger's EXTENSIVE CONSTANTS ARE STATED - GFR 180 L/day, CO 7200 mL/min, blood volume 5.0 L are textbook values for a roughly 70 kg, 1.73 m2 adult - so it is a normalisation convention belonging to those sources, NOT a claim about how much people weigh. It stays `both` and stays 70.0. The claim about people is BF.BODY_MASS.TYPICAL, which IS a male/female pair (90.3 / 77.9 kg, NHANES 2021-2023). Moving THIS row to a population mean would rescale every extensive constant against a denominator its own sources never used, turning GFR into 232 L/day by arithmetic rather than by measurement. The two rows are different quantities and ADR 0014 applies to each separately.

name: Typical adult body mass, population mean
citation: Fryar CD, Gu Q, Afful J, Carroll MD, Ogden CL. Anthropometric Reference Data for Children and Adults: United States, August 2021-August 2023. Vital and Health Statistics Series 3, No. 50. Atlanta (GA): National Center for Health Statistics; 2025 Jun. doi:10.15620/cdc/174595. Table 3, weight in kilograms for adults age 20 and older, by sex. Read from the NCBI Bookshelf reproduction of Table 3.
notes: NHANES TABLE 3, ADULTS AGE 20 AND OLDER. Male mean 90.3 kg (SEM 0.9, n = 2,688); female mean 77.9 kg (SEM 0.8, n = 3,254). Sample sizes unweighted, estimates weighted to the US population. Pregnant females excluded. Pre-registered in validation/body_mass_prereg.md, committed at 3fd859b before the source was opened. pooling_rule = single-source, k = 1. THIS IS NOT THE SAME QUANTITY AS BF.BODY_MASS.REFERENCE AND MUST NOT BE MERGED WITH IT. The reference row is the mass at which this ledger's EXTENSIVE CONSTANTS are stated - GFR 180 L/day, cardiac output 7200 mL/min, blood volume 5.0 L are all textbook values for a roughly 70 kg, 1.73 m2 adult. It is a normalisation convention belonging to those sources, not a claim about how much people weigh. THIS row is a claim about how much people weigh. Setting the reference to 90.3 would scale GFR to 232 L/day by construction, which is not a measurement of anything - it would restate the same physiology against a different denominator and silently rescale every constant whose source assumed 70 kg. The prereg said the sexed pair 'must move the model'. It moves the POPULATION, which is where body mass actually lives; the single-individual default stays at the reference so that no existing result moves for a reason unrelated to this extraction. WHAT THIS EXPOSES, AND IT IS NOT SMALL: a typical US adult male at 90.3 kg is 1.29x the reference mass, and scaling.jl already records that linear-in-mass scaling OVERSTATES the spread of GFR and cardiac output, which are properly normalised to body surface area. Applying linear scaling out to 1.29x is using it at the edge of where it is defensible. The US adult population this describes has a mean BMI in the obese range, so the model's typical individual is now heavier than the lean reference adults in whom GFR0 and CO0 were characterised. That is a real limitation of using a population survey as a physiological reference and it is recorded rather than hidden.

name: Adult body mass, 5th percentile
citation: Fryar CD, Gu Q, Afful J, Carroll MD, Ogden CL. Anthropometric Reference Data for Children and Adults: United States, August 2021-August 2023. Vital and Health Statistics Series 3, No. 50. Atlanta (GA): National Center for Health Statistics; 2025 Jun. doi:10.15620/cdc/174595. Table 3, weight in kilograms for adults age 20 and older, by sex. Read from the NCBI Bookshelf reproduction of Table 3.
notes: NHANES Table 3 percentile, adults 20 and older, same source and extraction as BF.BODY_MASS.TYPICAL. Entered as a PERCENTILE, NOT converted to a standard deviation, and that is deliberate. The source reports a standard error of the MEAN and a percentile distribution; it does not report a population SD. Two standard estimators disagree materially because body weight is right-skewed - (P95-P05)/3.29 gives 21.6 kg for males while IQR/1.349 gives 18.7 kg, and the male mean 90.3 sits above the median 86.6 - so picking one AFTER seeing the numbers is exactly the unfalsifiable choice validation/pooling.md exists to prevent, and the pre-registration did not declare an SD estimator. NO SD IS ENTERED. The ensemble samples Sobol between these bounds, which is what sample_population actually does with its argument anyway - it only ever took the 1st and 99th percentiles of the distribution it was handed and sampled uniformly between them. KNOWN LIMITATION, now explicit rather than disguised by a Normal: the sampled population is UNIFORM over this range, not weight-distributed, so it over-represents the tails. Fixing that needs a declared distribution family and an SD estimator chosen in advance, which is its own pre-registration.

name: Relative amplitude of circadian modulation of renal sodium handling
citation: Kanabrocki EL, Scheving LE, Olwin JH, et al. Circadian variation in the urinary excretion of electrolytes and trace elements in men. Am J Anat 1983;166(2):121-148.
notes: STILL ASSUMED AT 0.25, AND NOW WITH THE CONFLICT RECORDED RATHER THAN A SINGLE SOURCE. A wide sweep of the circadian sodium literature found the amplitude genuinely contested. UPPER END: Kanabrocki 1983, 11 healthy adult males, 3-hourly urine over 27 h with cosinor analysis, found a statistically significant population rhythm for sodium and reported that for almost every element the increase from lowest to highest 3-hour group mean exceeded 100%. A peak-to-trough ratio of 2 corresponds to a cosinor amplitude of 0.33, and >100% is a lower bound, so this supports 0.33 or more. LOWER END: Peng 2021, 85 healthy Chinese adults, every voided specimen over 24 h with cosinor analysis, found URINARY SODIUM SHOWED NON-SIGNIFICANT PARAMETERS IN THE COSINOR MODEL and that the sodium rhythm was less significant than potassium. That is close to an amplitude of zero. 0.25 sits between them and is NOT a pooled estimate - pooling a significant and a non-significant result is not defensible. THE RHYTHM'S EXISTENCE IS BETTER SUPPORTED THAN ITS SIZE: see CIRC.RENAL_NA.ENDOGENEITY_MARKER. THE PROPER SOURCE HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AND NOT YET OBTAINED - Minors and Waterhouse 1990 provide normative ENDOGENOUS urinary sodium data from about 80 constant routines, which is exactly the unmasked quantity this parameter should carry. Get it before trusting any circadian sodium result.

name: Time of peak renal sodium excretion
citation: Ueno M, Kawasaki T, Uezono K, Omae T, Matsuoka M. Relationship of urinary kallikrein excretion to renal water and sodium excretion. Metabolism 1983;32(5):433-437.
notes: STILL ASSUMED AT 0.33 day, AND THE ACROPHASE IS CONTESTED TOO - the two best cosinor studies found are nearly ANTIPHASE. Ueno 1983, 20 healthy Japanese women on an ordinary diet, cosinor: acrophase of urinary sodium excretion at 16:55, i.e. late afternoon, closely tracking urine volume at 16:51 (r = 0.935). Under this component's convention with a 07:00 active-period start that is 0.41 day. Peng 2021, 85 healthy Chinese adults, cosinor: sodium excretion had a NOCTURNAL PEAK falling to its lowest around noon to afternoon - roughly the opposite. 0.33 day (about 15:00) is retained as a placeholder consistent with Ueno and inconsistent with Peng. It is NOT a compromise between them; there is no defensible compromise between antiphase estimates. Resolve with the Minors and Waterhouse constant-routine normative data before this parameter is used for anything.

name: Endogenous circadian amplitude of mean arterial pressure, relative
citation: Shea SA, Hilton MF, Hu K, Scheer FAJL. Existence of an endogenous circadian blood pressure rhythm in humans that peaks in the evening. Circ Res 2011;108(8):980-984.
notes: PRECISION: rounded to 2 significant figures on 2026-08-27. The sources do not support more, and carrying digits that do not exist forced the closure gate and the test suite to chase arithmetic noise. Derived rows inherit the significant figures of their inputs and are rounded to match; the closure tolerance was moved to 1e-3 in the same change, which is still an order of magnitude tighter than the 6% error that motivated that gate. || REPLACES CIRC.CV_MAP.DIP_FRACTION = 0.15, WHICH WAS THE WRONG QUANTITY BY ABOUT NINE TIMES AND ALSO THE WRONG PHASE. That parameter encoded the 10-20% NOCTURNAL AMBULATORY DIP as though it were the endogenous circadian driver. It is not. Degaute 1991 (31 healthy young men, ambulatory BP with simultaneous polysomnography) found RECUMBENCY AND SLEEP ACCOUNT FOR 65-75% OF THE NOCTURNAL DECLINE, concluding that posture and the wake-sleep transition are the major factors in the 24-h BP rhythm. THE ENDOGENOUS COMPONENT IS REAL BUT SMALL. Shea 2011 measured it under three complementary protocols in 28 normotensive adults - a 38-h constant routine and forced desynchrony at 28-h and 20-h sleep/wake cycles - and found significant circadian rhythms in all three with almost identical profiles: peak-to-trough 3-6 mmHg systolic and 2-3 diastolic. Converting through MAP = DBP + (SBP-DBP)/3 gives 2.33-4.00 mmHg peak-to-trough, so a cosinor amplitude of 0.0125 to 0.0215 of MAP. Midpoint adopted, range carried. DERIVED because the MAP conversion is arithmetic on reported SBP and DBP, not a reported MAP amplitude. LIVE CONTROVERSY, RECORDED NOT RESOLVED: Kerkhof 1998 (25 normotensives, 26-h constant routine, stated power >0.95) found NO significant endogenous BP rhythm, and Van Dongen 2001 replicated that absence five times in six subjects. Shea's forced-desynchrony design separates circadian from behavioural influence more strongly than a constant routine alone and is followed here, but the disagreement is genuine and this parameter should be treated as the weakest in the cardiovascular arm.

name: Time of peak mean arterial pressure
citation: Shea SA, Hilton MF, Hu K, Scheer FAJL. Existence of an endogenous circadian blood pressure rhythm in humans that peaks in the evening. Circ Res 2011;108(8):980-984.
notes: PRECISION: rounded to 3 significant figures on 2026-08-27. The sources do not support more, and carrying digits that do not exist forced the closure gate and the test suite to chase arithmetic noise. Derived rows inherit the significant figures of their inputs and are rounded to match; the closure tolerance was moved to 1e-3 in the same change, which is still an order of magnitude tighter than the 6% error that motivated that gate. || WAS 0.25 day (13:00) AND ASSUMED. Shea 2011 reports that all six peaks - systolic and diastolic across three protocols - occurred at a circadian phase corresponding to approximately 21:00, the biological evening. Under this component's convention that phase 0 is the start of the active period, taken as 07:00 for humans, 21:00 is 14 h later = 0.583333 day. DERIVED only in that clock time is converted to the component's phase convention. NOTE WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE MODEL: the ENDOGENOUS BP peak is in the EVENING, whereas the familiar ambulatory dip is NOCTURNAL. They are not the same rhythm and are not even in phase, which is the second reason the old dip-fraction parameterisation was wrong. Shea also reports the BP rhythm was unrelated in phase to those of cortisol, catecholamines, cardiac vagal modulation, heart rate or urine flow.

This row is DERIVED and is not independent of GFR: a smaller filtered load needs a smaller reabsorbed fraction to excrete the same 205 mEq/day. Re-deriving it was mandatory, not optional - leaving it at 0.9918651 would have broken sodium balance by about 18%. The excreted fraction 1 - FR_Na moved 0.0081349 -> 0.0095956. A derived value does not need a citation, it needs its DERIVATION stated and checkable, and searching for a source would have been answering a question this row is not asking. NO NEW GATE WAS ADDED. tools/check_closure.py already asserts exactly this identity under 'Na excretion == Na intake' - directive 1.10, do not add what already exists. IT IS NOT INDEPENDENT OF RN.GFR.NOMINAL. If GFR moves this MUST move with it by the same derivation; re-entering them separately would break sodium balance silently. Restored to 0.9918651. A small difference of two large numbers needs enough digits on the large numbers to leave the difference meaningful - that is not false precision, it is the arithmetic. This is the same failure recorded in the header of tools/check_closure.py, where rounding this row to 0.9915 gave 214.2 against 205. || PRECISION: rounded to 4 significant figures on 2026-08-27. name: Pressure natriuresis slope
citation: Guyton AC, Coleman TG, Granger HJ. Circulation: overall regulation. Annu Rev Physiol 1972;34:13-46.
notes: CHANGED 11.4 -> 8.4 ON 2026-09-03, on the owner's instruction, and 8.4 is the CONSTRAINT-CONSISTENT partner of the sourced volume gain rather than a second free choice. The human joint constraint is G_pn + 0.0594*G_anp = 50 per 100 mmol/day; with CV.ANP.NATRIURETIC_GAIN sourced at 700 that gives 8.4 exactly. 11.4 had paired with 650 and the mismatch was recorded on this row when 11.4 was entered - it predicted a chronic salt sensitivity just below the human window, which is what was measured, and 8.4 was predicted to land inside it. It does. || CHANGED 20.0 -> 11.4 ON 2026-09-03 ON THE OWNER'S EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION. This row had been parked at his decision since 2026-08-25 and the instruction discharges that. IT IS NOT ADR 0013'S PROPOSAL - that record proposes 51.0 on the human PRESSURE evidence alone and remains Proposed and unadopted. 11.4 is the JOINT estimate that follows from ADR 0010's volume-keyed path being sourced and turned on: the human data constrain the COMBINATION G_pn + 0.0594*G_anp = 50 per 100 mmol/day, and with G_anp identified independently by the acute route the pressure slope is what remains. || ARITHMETIC NOTE THAT MATTERS. 11.4 pairs with G_anp = 650. The entered CV.ANP.NATRIURETIC_GAIN is 700, and the same constraint at 700 gives 8.4. So 11.4 and 700 are NOT the matched pair and the combination is under-satisfied by about 3 units, which shows up as a chronic salt sensitivity above the human window. Recorded rather than silently reconciled, because reconciling it by moving either number after seeing the result is the circularity this row's own history is a warning about. || WHAT IT DOES, measured with julia --project=. validation/challenges.jl. See the session record; the acute limbs are barely affected because they are carried by the volume path, and the chronic limb moves because this row is what sets it. || THE PREVIOUS NOTE IS PRESERVED BELOW BECAUSE ITS EVIDENCE IS UNCHANGED. || CALIBRATED, not measured. VALUE UNCHANGED AT 20.0 - read the identifiability result below before altering it. Originating model: Guyton 1972 systems analysis; the EXISTENCE and steepness of pressure natriuresis is E1 and well replicated, this particular slope is a fitted constant that propagated through the modelling literature. FORM: LINEAR, AND NOW SOURCED. Roman RJ, Cowley AW Jr, Am J Physiol 1985, PMID 3970209 (rat, denervated, vasopressin/aldosterone/corticosterone/noradrenaline clamped) report the relation as the slope of a LINE, 2 uL/min/kidney/mmHg over RPP 90-160 mmHg. Osborn/Francisco/DiBona, Proc Soc Exp Biol Med 1981, independently report UNaV falling LINEARLY over dog RPP 137-55 mmHg. An earlier note in relations.csv called the curve 'markedly nonlinear'; that was asserted from memory and is RETRACTED. VALIDITY RANGE roughly 55-160 mmHg. RN.AUTOREG.UPPER was 180, outside that range; moved to 160 on 2026-08-21 and cited to the same paper. MAGNITUDE CROSS-CHECK: Mizelle HL et al, Hypertension 1993;22:102-110 (dog, split bladder, bilateral servo-control, 12 d - the cleanest isolation of pressure per se) gives 3.468 mmol/day/mmHg whole animal = 2.154e-4 of filtered load per mmHg against this row's 7.937e-4, so the calibrated value is 3.68x STEEPER than the animal datum on a scaling-free basis. That is the range in uncertainty_value; 5.43 is the Mizelle-consistent value. SINGLE SOURCE, k=1, DOG - per validation/pooling.md that is animal-derived, may not be pooled with a human value, and is recorded as a comparator rather than adopted. IDENTIFIABILITY (measured 2026-08-20 on IPE at 9a6fa42): this parameter ALONE fixes the model's salt sensitivity. At steady state excretion equals intake, so Na_excr = Na_filtered*(1-FR_Na) + G_pn*(MAP-MAP_ref) gives dMAP ~ d(intake)/G_pn, in which CV.VENOUS_RETURN.SENSITIVITY does not appear. Confirmed numerically: the 205->103 mEq/day step gives 4.934 mmHg at G_pn=20.0 and 15.698 mmHg at G_pn=5.43, while varying G_vr over 2880->600 at fixed G_pn=5.43 moves the shift only 15.698->12.403 and drives V_ecf to 9.889 L, below the 10 L floor asserted in test/runtests.jl. The residual departure from an exact 1/G_pn law is C_Na drift. CONSEQUENCE, correcting HANDOVER.md section 5 item 4: G_pn and G_vr are NOT jointly identified as one lumped loop gain. G_pn is identified by the salt-sensitivity shift and G_vr by ECF volume, separately. Adopting the Mizelle value in isolation re-balances nothing - it forces a 15.7 mmHg shift across a 102 mEq/day range, which is salt-sensitive-hypertensive behaviour, not normotensive. WHY THE GAP IS PROBABLY REAL RATHER THAN AN ERROR: IPE has NO volume-sensing natriuretic path. Seeliger et al, J Physiol 2004;559:939-951, servo-controlled RPP during saline loading in freely moving dogs with NO reduction in peak or cumulative natriuresis, and Bie 2018 (10.1152/ajpregu.00363.2017) argues excretion is keyed to extracellular volume rather than pressure. With ANP absent, all sodium regulation is forced through this one term, so an inflated G_pn is the expected COMPENSATION for the missing path. DO NOT lower this to 5.43 before a volume-sensing natriuretic path exists - doing so degrades the only behaviour the model has ever reproduced. Re-estimate G_pn and the ANP gain JOINTLY against digitised Mars500, as posteriors, not this value alone and not as a point value. || ADR 0013'S FALSIFIABLE TEST WAS RUN ON 2026-09-02 AND THE VALUE STAYS AT 20.0. Pre-registered in validation/ecf_salt_response_prereg.md; reproduce with python validation/ecf_salt_response_extract.py. ADR 0013 proposes 20.0 -> 51.0 on the human PRESSURE response and requires its volume test to pass BEFORE acceptance. It fails. van den Bosch 2021 (Physiol Rep 2021;9(24):e15103, PMID 34921521, n = 70 healthy men, 7 d per level, ECFV by iothalamate, intake verified by 24 h urinary sodium) gives dMAP/dV_ecf = 1.885 mmHg/L against the model's 9.80 at that cohort's 80.6 kg - a factor of 5.2 against a pre-registered failure threshold of 2, and it fails on all three volume proxies so it does not turn on the iothalamate space or the 1 kg = 1 L conversion. THE FAILURE IS NOT ABOUT THIS ROW. G_pn and CV.VENOUS_RETURN.SENSITIVITY are ORTHOGONAL, measured: an 8x change in G_vr moves the pressure response by 0.12% and moves the volume response exactly inversely. G_pn sets dMAP; G_vr sets dMAP/dV_ecf. So the human pressure data and the human volume data identify one parameter each with no cross-talk, and the pressure limb still supports 51. What the test shows is that ACCEPTING 51 ALONE WOULD MAKE THE VOLUME RESPONSE WORSE - from 1.26x too small at 20 to 3.2x too small at 51 - because dMAP is what this row moves and dV_ecf follows it down at a fixed, wrong ratio. DECLARED CONFLICT: Heer 2000 (PMID 10751219) and Heer 2009 (PMID 19173770) report no total-body-water or body-mass increase on high sodium and a non-monotonic ECV response, which would put the error's sign the other way; that camp invokes osmotically inactive sodium storage, which is ADR 0004 and is default OFF here.

name: Lower limit of renal autoregulation
citation: Finke R, Gross R, Hackenthal E, Huber J, Kirchheim HR. Threshold pressure for the pressure-dependent renin release in the autoregulating kidney of conscious dogs. Pflugers Arch 1983;399(2):102-110. PMID 6139786. Lower limit of renal blood flow autoregulation, measured directly by servo-controlled stepwise reduction of renal artery pressure in the conscious animal.
notes: VALUE CHANGED 80.0 -> 63.9 mmHg ON 2026-08-27, AND SPECIES CORRECTED human -> dog. The previous value was NOT SOURCED: citation read 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.', which is not a reference, and species read 'human', which was not supported. This row was the last of the seven rows carrying that identical non-citation to be flagged as genuine debt rather than discharged, and HANDOVER 3.1 named it the one to look at first because CV.MAP.SETPOINT moved 93 -> 87 on the same day, carrying the operating point TOWARD this breakpoint. PRE-REGISTERED EXTRACTION: validation/autoreg_lower_prereg.md, committed at 3fbe260 BEFORE any paper was opened; executed by validation/autoreg_lower_extract.py. 26 PubMed queries in two sweeps, 1114 unique records screened. POOLING RULE, DECLARED BEFORE EXTRACTION per validation/pooling.md: single-source, n_studies k=1. No cross-species pooling was performed and no range midpoint was taken; both are prohibited for new entries. BRANCH 7 OF THE PRE-REGISTERED PROCEDURE WAS TAKEN. Branches 1-5 fail: NO human primary study reports a numeric lower breakpoint. The one that appears to - Textor SC et al, Ann Intern Med 1985;102(3):308-314, 'Critical perfusion pressure for renal function' - measures a STENOSIS threshold in bilateral atherosclerotic renovascular disease, not the intrinsic breakpoint of a normal kidney, and the sensitivity disappeared after revascularisation. Branch 6 fails too, and that is the finding of this pass: THE HUMAN EVIDENCE CONFLICTS AT THE SAME PRESSURE. At MAP 60 mmHg, Lessard MR and Trepanier CA, Anesthesiology 1991;74(5):860-865 (n=20, GFR by inulin, ERPF by PAH, MAP 59.8 +/- 0.4 for 237 min) found GFR not significantly further reduced and renal vascular resistance FALLING to maintain renal blood flow - the autoregulatory signature; while Hara T et al, J Clin Anesth 1998;10(7):539-545 (n=26, MAP 60 for 120 min) found creatinine clearance SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED in both arms. Lessard is the methodologically stronger study, but choosing it after seeing both is precisely what pre-registration forbids, so branch 6's condition - that human studies ESTABLISH preservation - genuinely fails on its own terms. There is no lower pressure where the human evidence is unconflicted either: at MAP 50, Zayas VM et al, Am J Physiol 1993;265(5 Pt 2):F686-F692 and Toivonen J et al, Eur J Anaesthesiol 1991;8(1):13-20 both report renal function falling. ALL FOUR HUMAN STUDIES ARE ANAESTHESIA SAFETY STUDIES and directive 1.7 predicts what they returned: apply the test - had the physiology come out differently, the conclusion would have been 'this hypotensive technique is unsafe for the kidney'. The pressure-flow relationship is the INSTRUMENT there, not the subject, and every one of them carries a confound (volatile anaesthetic, sympathetic blockade, vasodilator, or all three), with anaesthesia depressing GFR before any pressure was lowered. THE ADOPTED SOURCE IS THE OPPOSITE KIND OF STUDY. Finke 1983 varied renal artery pressure from 160 to 40 mmHg in seven CONSCIOUS foxhounds under beta-blockade on a normal sodium diet (4.1 mmol/kg/day), reducing it in steps held constant by a servo-control system driving an inflatable renal artery cuff. Between 160 mmHg and resting pressure renal blood flow did not change; between resting pressure and the lower limit of autoregulation, average 63.9 mmHg, it rose only about 7%. The relationship IS the subject. No standard deviation is reported for the limit itself, so uncertainty_type stays none rather than inventing one - the paper does report 89.8 +/- 3.3 mmHg for its separate renin threshold, so the omission is the authors' and not a transcription loss. DECLARED CONFLICTS, LOGGED AND NOT RESOLVED. (1) Shipley RE, Study RS, Am J Physiol 1951;167(3):676-688, PMID 14903093 - the ANAESTHETISED dog study that is the origin of the textbook 80-180 and therefore of the value this row carried; its PubMed record carries the MeSH term 'Humans', a legacy-indexing artefact of the AJP back catalogue already flagged in autoreg_upper_prereg.md. Anaesthesia is the most likely single explanation of 80 vs 63.9. (2) Cupples WA, Braam B, Am J Physiol Renal Physiol 2007;292(4):F1105-F1123, PMID 17229679 - a tier B review putting the limit at ~75 mmHg in dog and ~85 in rat. pooling.md: the primary source wins and the divergence is logged. Averaging 75 and 85 would produce a number describing neither species. (3) The 2025 human review already cited in this row's previous note (doi 10.22514/sv.2025.001) holds that human evidence is insufficient for 80 as the lower limit; this extraction agrees and goes further - the human evidence that does exist puts the limit near 60. THE BRANCH CHOICE IS NOT LOAD-BEARING: branch 6 would have given 59.8 and branch 7 gives 63.9, a 4.1 mmHg difference, and no conclusion depends on which. Two independent lines - conscious dog with a measured breakpoint, anaesthetised humans bracketing 50 to 60 - different species, designs, decades and authors, both land near 60. NEITHER SUPPORTS 80. NO MODEL RESULT CHANGES. The three salt arms sit at MAP 81.900 / 84.450 / 87.001 mmHg, above the old 80 and above the new 63.9, so all remain on the autoregulation plateau and every steady state is bit-identical. The pre-registration declared this BEFORE extraction so that 'it does not change the answer' could not wave the change through, and so that a value above ~81.9 would have had to be escalated rather than quietly avoided. WHAT CHANGES IS MARGIN: the low-salt arm sat 1.9 mmHg above a piecewise kink and now sits 18.0 mmHg above it. STILL DEBT, AND THE REASON IS FIXED IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION. This is a dog number and the human experiment IS performable - humans have repeatedly been taken to 50-60 mmHg. The ethical-ceiling argument that earns RN.AUTOREG.UPPER its E2 standing under the ADR 0006 amendment does NOT transfer to this row, and was ruled out in the pre-registration before the search so it could not be reached for afterwards. What is missing is a study that lowers pressure in humans WITHOUT general anaesthesia and measures GFR by inulin at graded steps. Debt with a named primary source is a real improvement on a non-citation; it is not a closure. NOT CHANGED HERE. Recorded because that row is the rectification point HANDOVER 3.1 found the model sitting exactly on, and a second independent primary source for it now exists in a paper this repo has read. THE PIECEWISE FORM REMAINS UNSOURCED: relations.csv row Renal.GFR keeps an empty form_citation and stays in GRANDFATHERED_UNSOURCED. A NUMBER was sourced, not an EQUATION. Finke in fact reports renal blood flow rising ~7% below resting pressure rather than staying flat, so the true plateau has a slight slope the model's ifelse does not represent.

name: Upper limit of renal autoregulation
citation: Roman RJ, Cowley AW Jr. Characterization of a new model for the study of pressure-natriuresis in the rat. Am J Physiol 1985;248:F190-F198. PMID 3970209. Highest renal perfusion pressure at which GFR was measured and found unchanged.
notes: EVIDENCE UNDER AN ETHICAL CEILING, NOT DEBT (ADR 0006 amended 2026-08-21). The rat provenance of this value is not a deficiency to be burned down. No human study raises arterial pressure to locate the failure of GFR autoregulation and none may; the human literature only ever lowers it. Where the human experiment cannot ethically exist, a well-conducted animal study is the evidence, not a substitute for it. This row is E2 with species, preparation and tested range recorded. WHAT REMAINS A REAL LIMITATION IS THE CENSORING, NOT THE SPECIES: 160 mmHg was the highest RPP tested in that preparation, so the true breakpoint is >= 160 and is not known to BE 160. UPPER BREAKPOINT MOVED 180 -> 160 mmHg ON 2026-08-21. The previous value was NOT SOURCED: citation read 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' and species read 'human', neither of which was true. POOLING RULE, DECLARED BEFORE EXTRACTION per validation/pooling.md, pre-registration in validation/autoreg_upper_prereg.md: single-source, n_studies k=1. The pre-registration fixed, before any paper was read, that if zero HUMAN primary studies reported an upper breakpoint then the value could not be retained by cross-species pooling or by range-midpoint (both prohibited) and had to be brought inside the range where the model's own relations have support. SEARCH RESULT - THERE IS NO HUMAN PRIMARY EVIDENCE FOR AN UPPER BREAKPOINT. PubMed yields no human study that RAISES arterial pressure and measures the pressure at which GFR autoregulation fails; for obvious reasons the human literature only ever probes the LOWER limb by LOWERING pressure - Parving HH et al, Diabetologia 1984;27:547-552 (clonidine, MAP fall 16-18 mmHg, PMID 6442240), New JP et al, Diabetologia 1998;41:206-211 (trandolapril, MAP 103->93, PMID 9498655), Christensen PK et al, Kidney Int 2001 (PMID 11576357) and Diabetes Care 2003 (PMID 12502673). None of these reaches 160 mmHg, let alone 180. WHERE 180 ACTUALLY CAME FROM: Shipley RE, Study RS, Am J Physiol 1951;167:676-688, doi 10.1152/ajplegacy.1951.167.3.676, PMID 14903093 - DOG, acute alterations of renal artery pressure. That is the primary origin of the textbook '80-180 mmHg' and it is canine. (The PubMed MeSH record for PMID 14903093 carries the term 'Humans'; that is a known legacy-indexing artefact of the AJP back-catalogue, contradicted by the paper and by every secondary source that cites it as the canine range. Recorded here because the MeSH tag would otherwise look like human support.) 180 therefore entered this ledger as a dog number wearing a human label. WHAT IS ADOPTED: Roman RJ, Cowley AW Jr, Am J Physiol 1985;248:F190-F198, doi 10.1152/ajprenal.1985.248.2.F190, PMID 3970209. RAT, denervated kidney, vasopressin, aldosterone, corticosterone and noradrenaline clamped by infusion, RPP set by aortic clamp. Verbatim: 'Increasing RPP within the autoregulatory range from 90 to 160 mmHg produced 5- to 20-fold increases in urine flow and sodium excretion with no detectable changes in glomerular filtration rate, renal blood flow, or peritubular capillary pressure.' That is a direct primary measurement that GFR autoregulation is INTACT at 160 mmHg. THIS IS A CENSORED OBSERVATION, NOT A MEASURED BREAKPOINT. 160 mmHg is the highest RPP Roman and Cowley tested, so the true upper limit is >= 160; it is not known to BE 160. uncertainty_type is 'none' rather than a range because inventing a 160-180 interval would smuggle back the range-midpoint reasoning pooling.md prohibits. The model breakpoint is set at the edge of evidence, which is the conservative direction: it makes GFR fall with pressure slightly earlier than reality, rather than asserting a flat plateau in a region nothing has measured. WHY 160 AND NOT SOMETHING ELSE - THE TWO CONSTRAINTS COINCIDE. Roman and Cowley 1985 is ALSO the form source for the model's pressure natriuresis (see RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE and ledger/relations.csv row Renal.FR_effective), where the LINEAR form is evidenced over roughly 55-160 mmHg. At 180 the autoregulation breakpoint sat OUTSIDE the range over which the equation it modifies has any support, so the model contained a kink in a region where its own natriuresis term was unevidenced. Setting the breakpoint to 160 makes the autoregulatory plateau and the natriuresis validity range terminate together, at the same pressure, from the SAME primary paper. That is not a coincidence chosen after the fact - the <=160 ceiling was written into the pre-registration before extraction. CROSS-SPECIES POOLING NOT PERFORMED, as prohibited. The dog value (Shipley 1951) and the rat value (Roman 1985) are NOT averaged. One rat study is adopted; the dog study is recorded as provenance archaeology for the discarded 180, not as a co-estimate. CORROBORATION, RECORDED AS CONTEXT AND NOT POOLED: Cupples WA, Braam B, Am J Physiol Renal Physiol 2007;292:F1105-F1123, doi 10.1152/ajprenal.00194.2006, describe the plateau as spanning from ~75 mmHg (dogs) or ~85 mmHg (rats) to >160 mmHg - note '>160', an open upper bound, not a fixed 180. Carlstrom M, Wilcox CS, Arendshorst WJ, Physiol Rev 2015;95:405-511, doi 10.1152/physrev.00042.2012, quote the conventional 80-180 mmHg. Both are reviews (tier B) and neither adds human primary data on the upper limit. SPECIES CHANGED human -> rat. TIER CHANGED B -> A: per SOURCES.md, tier A includes 'peer-reviewed primary research in animal models, flagged as such with species noted'. The tier RISES because the source is now a primary measurement rather than an unnamed reference, while the species flag FALLS to rat. Those are two separate axes and both moved honestly. KNOWN LIMITATION: the model is human. A rat autoregulatory breakpoint is being used in a human model because no human number exists. This is species extrapolation and is flagged as such. NO NUMERICAL EFFECT AT THE OPERATING POINT: IPE runs at MAP ~88-93 mmHg, inside [80, 160], where GFR ~ GFR0 either way. Verified: the ADR 0007 salt-step result is unchanged. The change buys honesty and removes an unevidenced kink, not different behaviour. WHAT IS STILL NOT SOURCED: the piecewise-flat-then-proportional FORM of the autoregulation equation, including its derivative discontinuity at both breakpoints. Only the breakpoint VALUE is sourced here. ledger/relations.csv row Renal.GFR therefore remains in the grandfathered unsourced list in tools/check_relations.py and its form_citation stays empty. LEDGER SCHEMA DEBT: validation/pooling.md specifies pooling_rule, n_studies and pooling_notes as columns of this CSV. Those columns do not exist yet, so the rule is recorded in prose here, following the precedent already set by RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE. SCALING FROM RAT TO HUMAN: NO SCALING FACTOR IS APPLIED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE CLAIM, NOT AN OMISSION. This parameter is a PRESSURE (mmHg), an intensive variable, unlike the extensive quantities in this ledger (GFR, sodium excretion, blood volume) which would require allometric scaling by body or kidney mass. Mean arterial pressure in the conscious rat (~100-120 mmHg) and in the adult human (~93 mmHg here) are the same order of magnitude, and the autoregulatory plateau is generated by afferent-arteriolar myogenic tone and tubuloglomerular feedback, which are transmural-pressure-sensing mechanisms operating on the same pressure scale in both species rather than mass-dependent ones. Cupples and Braam 2007 report lower limits of ~75 mmHg (dog) and ~85 mmHg (rat) - a ~10 mmHg spread across a roughly 40-fold body-mass difference, which is the empirical evidence that this quantity does not scale with mass. The residual risk is therefore not a missing scale factor but genuine between-species difference in the breakpoint itself, of order 10 mmHg based on that spread, and it is unquantified in the upward direction because no species has been measured above 160 mmHg in this preparation. RE-FRAMED 2026-08-21 under the ADR 0006 amendment: an earlier version of this note treated 'not human' as a defect. It is not. What is genuinely unsourced here is the piecewise FORM of the autoregulation equation (see ledger/relations.csv row Renal.GFR) and the LOWER breakpoint - not this value's species.

name: Obligatory urine volume at maximal concentration
citation: Derived from RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD and ADH.URINE.OSM_MAX.
notes: DERIVED 2026-09-01, AND THIS IS THE INVERSION THE ROW ITSELF ASKED FOR. V_min = RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD / ADH.URINE.OSM_MAX = 600.0 / 982.0 = 0.611 L/day. Was 0.5, `assumed`, citation empty, from branch 6 of validation/verify_rows_prereg.md - whose note said the derivation in this ledger was probably inverted and that sourcing U_max and deriving this row was the right next move. It is now done, U_max is sourced from Tryding 1988, and the conventional 0.5 L/day was 18% low. THE MODEL HAD ALREADY INVERTED IT. Renal.jl records that V_min is deliberately no longer a parameter: since the urine solute load began tracking sodium excretion (2026-08-27) the floor is computed as Osm_load / U_max and varies with the salt arm. Nothing in src/ reads this row. tools/check_closure.py was its only consumer and was asserting the relationship in the OPPOSITE direction to the code it is supposed to be checking. That is fixed in the same change. TIER C, INHERITED FROM THE NUMERATOR AND NOT FROM THE DENOMINATOR. ADH.URINE.OSM_MAX is now tier A, but RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD = 600 mOsm/day is an unsourced conventional figure that RN.URINE.SOLUTE_NONNA already records as too low for a Western diet - typical measured totals are 700-900. A larger true load would raise this floor proportionally. The weakest input sets the tier. WHAT IT MEANS PHYSICALLY: with a 600 mOsm/day load and a true maximal urine concentration of 982 mOsm/kg, urine output cannot fall below 611 mL/day. The old pairing claimed 500 mL, which required a concentrating ability nobody has measured.

name: Cardiac output at rest
citation: Derived from CV.HR.NOMINAL and CV.SV.NOMINAL.
notes: DERIVED 2026-09-01, AND THE DEPENDENCY IS NOW THE RIGHT WAY ROUND. CO0 = HR0 * SV0 * 1440 / 1000 = 62.0 * 96 * 1.44 = 8570.88 L/day (5.95 L/min). Exact - no rounding, because a derived row that closes an identity must carry every digit, the lesson CV.SV.NOMINAL recorded when it held that position. WHAT THIS ROW WAS. 7200 L/day, a `both` row, `assumed` with an EMPTY citation since branch 6 of validation/verify_rows_prereg.md, carrying the conventional 5 L/min x 1440. Its own note said the dependency was backwards and named this as the fix: stroke volume is what echocardiography and CMR MEASURE, cardiac output is what they compute. That is now done. Pre-re-registered in validation/dependency_inversion_prereg.md, which was committed BEFORE any paper was opened and sits immediately before this change in main's history. NO COMMIT SHA IS CITED, DELIBERATELY - rebase-merge rewrites it and every such citation already in this ledger points at a commit main does not contain. Verify the ordering instead: git log --diff-filter=A -- validation/dependency_inversion_prereg.md. THE TEXTBOOK 5 L/min WAS LOW, WHICH IS DIRECTIVE 1.12 AGAIN. Measured stroke volume with measured supine resting heart rate gives 5.95 L/min in men and 4.88 in women, against a unisex conventional 5.00. Five of these rows have now been opened and the round number was materially wrong in five of them. TWO COHORTS, AND THAT IS INHERENT TO DERIVING A PRODUCT. SV0 is Petersen 2017 (UK Biobank CMR, 45-74) and HR0 is Gonzales 2023 (Fenland, supine chest sensor, 29-65). Both are supine resting measurements in health-screened adults, which is the condition this model means by nominal, but they are not the same people: Petersen's own cohort heart rate during scanning is 67-70 bpm, above Fenland's supine 63.5. Using Petersen's HR instead would give 6.4 L/min in men. The mismatch is real and is why this is `derived` rather than `reported`. OVERDETERMINATION, AND THE RULE THAT PREVENTS IT. CO = HR x SV is an identity, so at most two of the three may be sourced. HR0 and SV0 are; this one is derived. If a cardiac output is ever sourced directly it REPLACES one of them, it does not join them. NO uncertainty is carried here. The dispersion lives on SV0 (sd 20 / 14 mL) and HR0 (sd 8.9), and combining them would need their covariance, which neither source reports. The sd 1150 this row used to carry belonged to the 5 L/min convention and went with it.

name: Mean arterial pressure nominal
citation: Gomez-Sanchez M, Gomez-Sanchez L, Patino-Alonso C, Recio-Rodriguez JI, Alonso-Dominguez R, Sanchez-Aguadero N, Sanchez CL, Sanchez ER, Garcia-Ortiz L, Gomez-Marcos MA. Reference values of central blood pressure and central haemodynamic parameters and their relationship with cardiovascular risk factors in a Spanish population: early vascular ageing study. J Hypertens 2021;39(11):2147-2156.
notes: CHANGED 93.0 -> 87.0 ON 2026-08-27, AND THE OLD VALUE WAS A CATEGORY ERROR. 93 was the textbook BRACHIAL 120/80 convention - 80 + 40/3 = 93.33, matching to 0.3 mmHg - carried under the citation 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' It was never verified, and this is that verification failing. NOW DERIVED from the sourced CENTRAL pressure: MAP = DBP + PP/3 = 76 + 33/3 = 87.0, on 501 adults without cardiovascular disease, age- and sex-stratified random sample. WHY CENTRAL RATHER THAN BRACHIAL. Chemla's SV/PP compliance relation is defined on aortic pressure, so the reconstruction needs a central reference. Mixing a brachial MAP with a central pulse pressure produced a form factor of 0.515 - IMPOSSIBLE, since the fraction of pulse pressure above mean must be below 0.5 when diastole is longer than systole. That contradiction is what exposed the mixing. TRUE MEAN PRESSURE IS NEARLY AMPLIFICATION-INVARIANT: pulse pressure amplifies distally, mean pressure barely does. So there is one MAP, not a central and a brachial one, and the fixed 1/3 form factor giving 87 centrally and 89.8 brachially is an artefact of the formula rather than physiology - which is exactly what reconstruct.jl says about treating the form factor as constant. STILL AN INITIALISATION VALUE AND A VALIDATION TARGET, NOT A SETPOINT THE MODEL ENFORCES. Arterial pressure remains an output of the loop.

name: Total peripheral resistance nominal
citation: Derived from CV.MAP.SETPOINT and CV.CO.NOMINAL.
notes: RECOMPUTED AND SEXED 2026-09-01. TPR = MAP0 / CO0 = 87.0 / 8570.88 = 0.010151 mmHg/(L/day). Was 0.012083, a `both` row, because CO0 was a `both` row. CO0 became a male/female pair when stroke volume was sourced (Petersen 2017), so this row is dimorphic with it - as its own prior note and check_closure.py both said it would be. DEFINITIONAL GIVEN THE OTHER TWO. MAP is an OUTPUT of the closed loop; this is the resistance that makes the nominal operating point consistent, not a regulated setpoint. Because it is derived FROM MAP, arterial pressure at the operating point is unchanged by construction when CO0 moves - what moves is the volume excursion needed to produce a given pressure change, since dMAP/dV = TPR * G_vr. PRECISION: 5 significant figures, matching the 0.012083 it replaces. The identity closes to better than 1e-4 relative, an order of magnitude inside the 1e-3 closure tolerance. TPR CARRIES THE RECIPROCAL OF BODY SIZE in Cardiovascular.jl (TPR0 / sz) so that MAP stays intensive. See src/scaling.jl. That is unchanged.

name: Total blood volume nominal
citation: Oberholzer L, Montero D, Robach P, Siebenmann C, Ryrsoe CK, Bonne TC, Breenfeldt Andersen A, Bejder J, Karlsen T, Edvardsen E, Ronnestad BR, Hamarsland H, Cepeda-Lopez AC, Rittweger J, Treff G, Ahlgrim C, Almquist NW, Hallen J, Lundby C. Determinants and reference values for blood volume and total hemoglobin mass in women and men. Am J Hematol 2024;99(1):88-98. doi:10.1002/ajh.27162. PMID 38032792. Carbon monoxide rebreathing in 263 women and 319 men, age 10-93: blood volume 80.3 +/- 10.8 mL/kg body mass in men and 70.3 +/- 11.3 in women.
notes: CHANGED 5.0 L `both` -> 5.62 male / 4.92 female ON 2026-08-27, AND IT IS NOW A REAL DIMORPHISM. The previous value was NOT SOURCED: citation read 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' while extraction_method claimed `reported`. 5.0 L is the round teaching figure, like 120/80 and 37 degrees - a pedagogical convention, not a measurement. Pre-registered in validation/verify_rows_prereg.md at e0195f4 before any source was opened. pooling_rule = single-source, k = 1. THE VALUE: measured per kg of body mass, so it is entered at the reference mass. 80.3 mL/kg * 70 kg = 5.621 -> 5.62 L male; 70.3 * 70 = 4.921 -> 4.92 L female, 3 significant figures per directive 1.9. SD 10.8 and 11.3 mL/kg -> 0.76 and 0.79 L. n = 319 men and 263 women, ages 10-93, BMI 14-41, plus 107 athletes analysed separately. Because blood volume is reported PER KG, it composes correctly with src/scaling.jl, which already scales this row by body mass. THE SEX DIFFERENCE IS BODY COMPOSITION, NOT A SEPARATE MECHANISM, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO. Blood volume per kg BODY MASS is 25% lower in women, but per kg LEAN MASS it is 6% HIGHER (110.9 +/- 12.5 women against 105.3 +/- 11.2 men). Lean body mass was the strongest single predictor, R2 = 0.72. It does not, so the pair stands. DECLARED METHOD LIMITATION, IN THE AUTHORS' OWN WORDS: these values may only be valid for blood volume assessed by CO rebreathing. Cross-method comparison is prohibited by pooling.md and none was attempted. WHAT FOLLOWS FROM IT: CV.PLASMA.ECF_FRACTION and CV.CENTRAL.VOLUME_NOMINAL are DERIVED from this row and become sexed with it. The operating point does NOT move: f_pv is derived so that f_pv*V_ecf/(1-Hct) = BV0, and VC0 = f_c*BV0, so V_central - VC0 is unchanged at nominal, stroke volume is unchanged, and MAP is unchanged. What changes is that the blood volume is now a measurement instead of a round number. STILL RESTING ON UNSOURCED HAEMATOCRIT: f_pv is computed with CV.HEMATOCRIT.NOMINAL = 0.45, which is itself still one of the VERIFY rows and is expected to be dimorphic. name: Volume-keyed natriuretic gain
citation: ROUTE B, ACUTE ISOTONIC EXPANSION, TWO HUMAN STUDIES. Lobo DN, Stanga Z, Simpson JA, Anderson JA, Rowlands BJ, Allison SP. Clin Sci (Lond) 2001;101(2):173-9. PMID 11473492. 10 healthy men, 2 L of 0.9% saline over 1 h, double-blind crossover: 95 mmol urinary sodium over the 6 h after infusion, and a 7.5% fall in haematocrit which gives the intravascular share of the load DIRECTLY with red cell mass fixed. || Jensen JM, Mose FH, Bech JN, Nielsen S, Pedersen EB. BMC Nephrol 2013;14:202. PMID 24067081. 23 healthy subjects, randomised crossover on a standardised diet, 0.9% saline 23 mL/kg: fractional sodium excretion rose 123%. || CROSS-CHECKED against ROUTE A, the chronic steady-state constraint built from the meta-analytic human pressure response and the pooled human ECF response already extracted in this repo. || CORROBORATING the timescale: Drummer C, Heer M, Baisch F, Blomqvist CG, Lang RE, Maass H, Gerzer R. Acta Physiol Scand Suppl 1992;604:101-11. PMID 1324562. 6 healthy men, 22 mL/kg 0.9% saline: sodium excretion rose 3-fold, under 15% of the load was excreted acutely, and excretion stayed elevated beyond 48 h - the excretion of an acute isotonic load takes days, which is what this model does.
notes: RE-ESTIMATED 2026-09-03, 700 -> 585, AND THIS ROW'S OWN NOTE REQUIRED IT. It said: part of 700 compensates for a volume excursion 1.5-2.1x too large while CV.VENOUS_RETURN.SENSITIVITY is calibrated, so re-estimate when G_vr is sourced. G_vr was sourced in healthy humans on 2026-09-03 (2880 -> 1400, section 3.19), the caveat came due, and this is that re-estimation. NOT a new search - the same two human datasets, re-solved against corrected inputs. || THE PROCEDURE IS UNCHANGED AND THE IDENTIFICATION IS CLEAN. Two data, two parameters: the CHRONIC salt-step response fixes this gain, Lobo's 6 h ACUTE time course fixes RN.ANP.TAU. A first-order lag cannot move a steady state, so the two are separately identified - measured, not assumed: at G_anp 500/700/900 the chronic sensitivity is 2.275/1.720/1.382 regardless of tau, and 1/sensitivity is linear in the gain. || THE VALUE. Solved for a chronic salt sensitivity of 2.00 mmHg per 100 mmol/day, the CENTRE of the meta-analytic human 1.70-2.30 (Cutler 1997, He 2013, He 2002; k = 3). Verified by running rather than interpolating: 585 gives exactly 2.000. || WHAT IT NOW REPRODUCES, at G_pn = 8.4 and G_vr = 1400. Lobo 2001 (PMID 11473492): 566 mL and 95.1 mmol over the 6 h after 2 L of 0.9% saline, against a measured 563 and 95 - within 0.5 percent on both. READ THAT AS A FIT RESIDUAL AND NOT AS ACCURACY: RN.ANP.TAU WAS ESTIMATED AGAINST THIS SAME 6 H TIME COURSE, as the identification paragraph on this row says, so agreeing with it closely is what estimation is FOR rather than evidence that the model predicts anything. Corrected 2026-09-04, when HANDOVER was found claiming the four Lobo endpoints as validations in three places while section 3.21 said two paragraphs above that Lobo fixed the lag. The genuinely out-of-sample number is Jensen 2013, and it is a third low. What DOES survive here is an internal consistency check: the two Lobo endpoints imply the same lag independently, 0.171 d from the volume and 0.166 d from the sodium. Two endpoints of one protocol in the same subjects are not an independent test, and the acute limb of this model rests entirely on that one protocol class - Lobo and Jensen are both intravenous isotonic saline into healthy volunteers. Chronic salt sensitivity 2.000 against 1.70-2.30. dMAP/dV_ecf 3.000 mmHg/L against a measured human 2.97-4.16. || AND AN OUT-OF-SAMPLE CHECK THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN TUNED. Jensen 2013 (PMID 24067081) was NOT used in the estimation. The model predicts a peak fractional sodium excretion rise of 82.5% against the reported 123%. Inside the harness band and about a third low. That is the honest standing of this parameterisation on data it was not fitted to, and it is the sharpest remaining discrepancy in the sodium limb. || WHY THE GAIN FELL WHILE THE MODEL GOT BETTER. G_vr halving roughly doubled the model's volume excursion per unit intake, so a smaller gain now produces the same chronic natriuresis. 700 x 0.836 = 585, and the 0.836 is the correction the old note predicted would be needed. || SENSED VARIABLE, FORM AND EVIDENCE BASE ARE UNCHANGED - see the citation column and ADR 0010. name: Volume-keyed natriuresis time constant

citation: Morales-Mendoza E, Suarez-Ramos MDP, Godoy-Corredor M, Gomez-Lopera N, Combariza-Vallejo JF, Murcia J, Isaza-Ruget MA. notes: CHANGED 0.45 `both` -> 0.453 male / 0.395 female ON 2026-08-28. The previous value was NOT SOURCED: citation read 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' while extraction_method claimed `reported`. Pre-registered in validation/verify_rows_prereg.md at e0195f4. pooling_rule = single-source, k = 1. Verified empirically: entering this pair left every simulated result bit-identical. It will bite the moment f_pv is sourced independently - plasma volume as a fraction of extracellular volume is directly measurable - or when anything depending on viscosity or oxygen carriage exists. Until then this row is honest provenance for a quantity the model reports but does not yet use. || THIS ROW BECAME IDENTIFIABLE ON 2026-09-02, AND HANDOVER SECTION 3.5 SAID IT WOULD NOT. That section recorded haematocrit as non-identifiable: CV.PLASMA.ECF_FRACTION is DERIVED as BV0*(1-Hct)/V_ecf, so f_pv/(1-Hct) = BV0/V_ecf and this row cancelled out of every result - verified empirically at the time, a 15% sex difference leaving every output identical to seven figures. THAT CANCELLATION IS IN THE LEVEL ONLY. Cardiovascular.jl computed V_blood as V_plasma/(1-Hct) with Hct constant, which makes red cell volume expand with plasma; over a 30 day salt step red cell mass is fixed, so that was wrong. The equation is now V_blood ~ V_plasma + Hct*BV0, and the DERIVATIVE dV_blood/dV_ecf is f_pv = BV0*(1-Hct)/V_ecf0, which depends on this row. The sourced 0.453/0.395 pair now moves a result: the male/female ECF excursion ratio goes 1.069 -> 1.182, and the part that is new is entirely haematocrit because it is the only term that stopped cancelling. Section 3.9 records a whole line of work withdrawn for composing a compliance and a resistance into it while treating right atrial pressure as fixed. Blood volume can be changed by a KNOWN amount in healthy people - withdrawal, or plasma expansion - and cardiac output measured, so the composite is directly measurable in a performable paradigm. || THE VALUE, from the resting withdrawal limb. Diaz-Canestro C, Pentz B, Sehgal A, Montero D. Appl Physiol Nutr Metab 2022;47(1):75-82, PMID 34875180: 30 healthy women aged 47-77, non-smokers, non-obese, blood volume 3.8-6.6 L; a standard 10% reduction of blood volume (0.5 +/- 0.1 L withdrawn, haematocrit unchanged) reduced left ventricular end-diastolic volume and stroke volume by at least 10% AT REST, P <= 0.009. On a female cardiac output of 4.88 L/min that is 0.98 (L/min)/L = 1404 (L/day)/L, entered as 1400. The paper's title is 'in proportion to induced hypovolemia' - the relationship IS the subject, directive 1.7. || IT IS AN UPPER BOUND AND IS ENTERED AS ONE. A study reporting STROKE volume bounds dCO/dV from above, because heart rate can compensate; the pre-registration said so before the search. Three expansion studies all indicate the true resting value is at or below it and none resolves how far: Bundgaard-Nielsen 2010 (PMID 20545713, n=20 healthy supine) gave 200 mL of colloid and NO subject raised stroke volume by 10%, with cardiac output and heart rate both unchanged; Nguyen 1988 (PMID 2901018, n=8 healthy men) expanded intravascular volume 10-11% with hypertonic saline for small NON-SIGNIFICANT changes in stroke volume and cardiac index; Kanstrup 1982 (PMID 7096143) found cardiac output rose after 700 mL but reports no resting magnitude. || ASYMMETRY, MEASURED, AND IT NEARLY FAILED THE PRE-REGISTERED TEST. Fortney SM, Wenger CB, Bove JR, Nadel ER. J Appl Physiol 1983;55(3):884-90, PMID 6629925 is the only study giving BOTH limbs in the SAME 5 healthy men under the same protocol: -490 mL gave -2.2 L/min and +440 mL gave +1.0 L/min, i.e. 4.49 against 2.27 (L/min)/L, a ratio of 1.98 against a failure threshold of 2 fixed before the numbers. It passes by 1 percent. A LINEAR SYMMETRIC GAIN IS AT THE EDGE OF WHAT THIS EVIDENCE SUPPORTS, and the direction is the expected one - the heart sits nearer the flat part of its filling curve above normovolemia than below. Those figures are at 65-70 percent of VO2max and are recorded as evidence about the FORM; the pre-registration fixed that resting values govern, because the salt step is a resting protocol. || TWO INDEPENDENT LINES AGREE AND THAT IS THE RESULT. Chronic sodium balance implies 1012-1941 (HANDOVER 3.7, 3.8) from human pressure and volume responses. Acute volume manipulation in healthy people gives 1400. The two share no data, no subjects, no measurement and no timescale. THE MODEL WAS 2.06x TOO STIFF, which is inside the 1.5-2.1x that section 3.7 estimated from the salt data alone. || NOT CIRCULAR, AND CHECKABLE. The pre-registration forbade choosing a value to land the salt step in the human window, because the salt data are the TEST and may not also be the estimator. 1400 does NOT land it in the window; a value chosen to pass would have been nearer 1700. || STILL UNSOURCED IN HEALTHY HUMANS: systemic venous compliance in mL/mmHg, mean systemic filling pressure, and resistance to venous return. THE MODEL IS 5.2x TOO STIFF ON PRESSURE PER UNIT VOLUME. This is measurable independently of G_pn: an 8x change in this row moves the salt-step PRESSURE response by 0.12% while moving the VOLUME response exactly inversely, so the two parameters are orthogonal and each is identified by its own human datum. DO NOT SIMPLY REFIT IT TO 554. This row is `calibrated` and HANDOVER section 4 item 1 is to REPLACE it with sourced venous compliance - Pmsf, right atrial pressure, stressed versus unstressed volume. 554 is the target that work now has to explain, not a value to enter; entering it would swap one fitted constant for another and lose the falsifiable test in the process. DECLARED CONFLICT: Heer 2000 and Heer 2009 report no body-mass or total-body-water rise on high sodium, which would reverse the sign of this discrepancy. See ADR 0013. || EVIDENCE BASE WIDENED THE SAME DAY, AND THE TARGET IS A RANGE, NOT 554. Two further sweeps (24 queries, 162 records) because the verdict rested on one cohort. The body-weight limb now has FOUR independent groups - van den Bosch 2021 (n=70, 0.729 kg/100 mmol), Rorije 2018 (Anesthesiology 2018;128(2):352-360, PMID 29206647, n=12, +2.5 kg 95% CI 1.7-3.2 with blood pressure UNCHANGED), Foo 1998 (Clin Sci 1998;95(2):157-164, PMID 9680497, n=18, +0.45 +/- 0.69 kg) and Heer 2000 (n=32, no increase, entered as zero and that is an interpretation of a null). n-weighted pooled 0.572 kg/100 mmol over n=132, or 0.755 excluding Heer. THE TRACER LIMB GIVES 0.553 L, so two independent methods agree to 4% and the pre-registered 1 kg = 1 L conversion is corroborated rather than assumed - prereg section 8 said it would be falsified if they diverged. Pairing the META-ANALYTIC pressure (1.70-2.30 mmHg/100 mmol) with the pooled volume gives 2.97-4.16 mmHg/L, so the model is 2.7-3.8x too stiff and G_vr's target is 758-1062; the within-subject van den Bosch pair gives 5.2x and 554 as the harshest reading. USE THE POOLED RANGE: the mechanistic volume studies are underpowered for the 2 mmHg the meta-analyses detect - Kirkendall 1976 (PMID 1249473, n=8, FOUR WEEKS per level, the closest protocol to this model's 30 days), Rorije 2018 and Taurio 2023 (PMID 36708156, n=510, the largest dataset found) all report NO blood pressure change at all, and taking that at face value would drive this row to zero. PART OF THE DISCREPANCY IS NOT THIS ROW: Cardiovascular.jl computes V_blood as V_plasma/(1-Hct) with Hct constant, so red cell volume expands with plasma over a 30 day salt step when red cell mass is fixed. dV_blood/dV_ecf should be f_pv = 0.211, not f_pv/(1-Hct) = 0.386 - a factor of 1.83 that would take the model ratio to 6.17 and leave this row needing only 1.5-2.8x, i.e. about 1000-1950. DIAGNOSED, NOT YET RUN. || TARGET REVISED 2026-09-02 AFTER THE RED CELL CORRECTION: 1012-1941, NOT 758-1062. Cardiovascular.jl stopped letting red cell volume expand with plasma, which moved dMAP/dV_ecf from 11.285 to 6.173 and closed 1.83x of the discrepancy on its own. The residual attributable to THIS row is therefore 1.5-2.1x rather than 2.7-5.2x. Required ratio 2.97-4.16 mmHg/L at the 70 kg reference gives 2880 * ratio / 6.173 = 1385-1941, or 1012 on the harshest within-subject reading. AND THE ENDPOINT IS NOW MEASURED: with G_pn = 51 (ADR 0013) AND this row near 1400 the model returns dMAP = 1.944 mmHg and dV_ecf = 0.648 L per 100 mmol/day at a ratio of 3.001, against human 1.70-2.30, 0.553-0.572 and 2.97-4.16 - inside all three at once. NEITHER CORRECTION ALONE LANDS: ADR 0013 alone gives the right pressure with dV 0.315 (1.8x too small), and this row alone gives the right ratio with dMAP 4.958 (2.5x too large). DO NOT ENTER 1400. It is illustrative. This row must be REPLACED by sourced venous compliance, and that table is the target the sourced relation has to EXPLAIN.

name: Sympathetic arterial baroreflex open-loop gain
citation: Yamasaki F, Sato T, Sato K, Diedrich A. Analytic and integrative framework for understanding human sympathetic arterial baroreflex function. Front Neurosci 2021;15:707345.
notes: SPECIES: animal (dog, rabbit) - open-loop gain measured by perfusing vascularly isolated carotid sinus or aortic arch, reported between 1.0 and 3.5 across Kent 1972, Shoukas and Sagawa 1973, McRitchie 1976, Burattini 1994, Sato 1999, Sunagawa 2001. The source states explicitly that this invasive approach is not applicable to humans and that human open-loop gain has NOT been clarified. 2.0 is the mid-range. NO SCALING APPLIED - gain is dimensionless and the reflex architecture is conserved, but this is the weakest link in the component and must be flagged in any result.

name: Sympathetic vasomotor effector time constant
citation: La Rovere MT, Pinna GD, Raczak G. Baroreflex sensitivity: measurement and clinical implications. Ann Noninvasive Electrocardiol 2008;13(2):191-207.
notes: Cardiac and vasomotor sympathetic activation occurs with a 2-3 second delay and reaches maximal effect more slowly. Parasympathetic activation is far faster (200-600 ms) but acts on heart rate, which is not a state in this cycle-averaged model (ADR 0002) - hence the lumped single-arm treatment. 3.0 s is the upper end of the stated range.

name: Baroreflex setpoint resetting time constant
citation: Dampney RAL. Resetting of the baroreflex control of sympathetic vasomotor activity during natural behaviors. Front Physiol 2017.
notes: ASSUMED. Baroreflex resetting is well established qualitatively - the reflex re-centres on prevailing pressure over hours to days, which is WHY it cannot set long-run arterial pressure. A specific human time constant is not reported in the sources consulted. 1 day is an order-of-magnitude placeholder. CRITICAL: this parameter is what makes the baroreflex a fast buffer rather than a long-term regulator. If it were infinite the reflex would set long-run pressure and the Guyton claim in ADR 0007 would be false. Sensitivity to it must be tested.

name: Maximum fractional change in TPR from baroreflex
citation: Saturation bound; see notes.
notes: ASSUMED. The baroreflex characteristic is sigmoidal and saturates; an unbounded linear gain would let TPR go negative under large pressure excursions. 0.5 means TPR can move at most +/-50 percent from baseline by reflex action alone. Placeholder chosen to keep the model well-posed under hemorrhage-scale perturbations, not extracted from a reported response range.

name: Central (intrathoracic) blood volume as fraction of total
notes: PLACEHOLDER, NOT SOURCED, AND INERT AT ADR 0012 STAGE 1. Do not quote this number anywhere. Stage 1 introduces the central/peripheral partition as a change of variables only: CV.CENTRAL.CO_SENSITIVITY and CV.CENTRAL.VOLUME_NOMINAL are both derived from this value so that it cancels out of the CO relation algebraically. A non-power-of-two placeholder is equally correct algebraically but noisier. IT MUST BE SOURCED UNDER A PRE-REGISTRATION BEFORE STAGE 2, when f_central becomes posture-dependent and stops cancelling. At that point this row is load-bearing and this note must be replaced, not amended.
