name: Renal perfusion pressure above which renin release plateaus
citation: van Ochten M, El Fathi W, Bovee EME, Spaanderman MEA, Hooijmans CR, van Drongelen J. The renal baroreflex: a systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy and hypertensive animals. Physiol Rep 2025;13(17):e70547.
notes: THE COINCIDENCE IS BROKEN AS OF 2026-08-27, AND IT WAS THE FRAGILITY THIS ROW WARNED ABOUT. This threshold, 93 mmHg from van Ochten, used to equal CV.MAP.SETPOINT exactly, so the model sat ON the rectification point and RAAS was inactive at baseline BY CONSTRUCTION. The note said that rested on one unverified number. It did: the setpoint was the textbook brachial 120/80 convention and is now 87.0, derived from sourced central pressure. The model therefore sits 6 mmHg BELOW threshold and RAAS IS NOW ACTIVE AT REST - renin drive 0.069, plasma renin activity 2.31x baseline. That is more physiological, not less: resting renin is not zero. || Meta-analysis of 30 animal studies: renin falls linearly with rising renal pressure and plateaus above 93 +/- 2 mmHg. ADR 0006 E2 - servo-controlling renal perfusion pressure is not performable in humans, the same ethical ceiling as RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE. QUALITY CAVEAT FROM THE PAPER ITSELF: risk of bias was high in most studies. FRAGILITY, RECORDED: this threshold equals CV.MAP.SETPOINT = 93.0, whose own citation reads 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' The model therefore sits exactly ON the rectification threshold and RAAS is inactive at and above baseline BY CONSTRUCTION. That coincidence is doing structural work and rests on one unverified number. Verified against PubMed record PMID 40930784 on 2026-08-25. SCALING: none applied, and none is needed. The quantity is a PRESSURE THRESHOLD in mmHg, and arterial pressure is not body-size scaled across the mammals in this meta-analysis the way a flow or a volume would be - the threshold is reported in the same units the model uses. What is assumed instead is that the threshold TRANSFERS to humans unchanged, which is a species assumption rather than a scaling one, and it is the assumption to attack if this component misbehaves. Note the meta-analysis itself found the threshold comparable between healthy and hypertensive animals while the slope differed, which is weak evidence that the threshold is the more transferable of the two.

name: Aldosterone response to renin activity, log-log slope
citation: Walker WG, Moore MA, Horvath JS, Whelton PK. Arterial and venous angiotensin II in normal subjects. Circ Res 1976;38(6):477-483.
notes: DERIVED: log(5)/log(20) = 0.5372, from a 5-fold aldosterone rise against a 20-fold PRA rise across sodium restriction plus furosemide versus sodium surfeit, 16 normal subjects. COMPRESSIVE - a power law with exponent below 1. THE EXPONENT IS AGAINST PRA, NOT ANGIOTENSIN II. The parked component docstring said 'aldosterone vs angiotensin'; Walker reports a 2.72-fold arterial AngII rise, so aldosterone against AngII is log-log 1.47 and EXPANSIVE. Attaching the PRA-derived exponent to an angiotensin variable would have been wrong, and the model state is named pra for that reason. Verified against PMID 773568 on 2026-08-25.

name: Time constant of escape from mineralocorticoid sodium retention
citation: Kelly TM, Nelson DH. Sodium excretion and atrial natriuretic peptide levels during mineralocorticoid administration. Endocr Res 1987;13(4):363-383.
notes: DERIVED from the reported time course, not read off directly. Urinary sodium fell 27% immediately on fludrocortisone and returned to baseline levels in an average of 5 days, in four healthy males at 180 +/- 2 mEq/day. Modelling that as first-order recovery reaching 95% at 5 days gives tau = 5/ln(20) = 1.669 day. THE 95% CONVENTION IS A CHOICE and is recorded as one; 5/3 is within 0.1% of it. n=4, single study, so this is the weakest link in the escape path. Attribution was corrected once already, from 'Yokota N et al.' on 2026-08-21; re-verified against PMID 2966064 on 2026-08-25 and authors and every quoted number check out.

name: Time constant of the renin response to a pressure step
notes: ASSUMED, and deliberately not cited. The parked component attributed renin kinetics to Hofbauer KG et al. Pflugers Arch 1975; that paper was NOT opened, so per directive 1.5 it is not recorded here. 0.0035 day is about 5 minutes. WHY THE VALUE BARELY MATTERS: it is three orders of magnitude faster than the escape time constant and four faster than the renal-body fluid loop, so on this timebase the renin step is effectively instantaneous and any value in the minutes range gives the same trajectory. If it is ever made to matter, source it first. ADR 0002 would also justify making pra algebraic and dropping the state entirely.

name: Fractional renin rise per fractional fall in perfusion pressure
citation: van Ochten M, El Fathi W, Bovee EME, Spaanderman MEA, Hooijmans CR, van Drongelen J. The renal baroreflex: A systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy and hypertensive animals. Physiol Rep 2025;13(17):e70547. doi:10.14814/phy2.70547. PMID 40930784. PMC12422813. THE SLOPE, section 3.3.2 and Figure 6, read as full text: 'A decrease of 10 mmHg in renal blood pressure leads to an increase of 50 percentage points renin in healthy animals', where renin is expressed as a percentage of the value at the baseline mean renal arterial pressure of 110 mmHg, set to 100%. That baseline is ABOVE the 93 mmHg threshold, so the 100% reference IS the plateau - which is exactly what pra = 1 means in Raas.jl. Slope = 0.05 of plateau renin per mmHg.
notes: RE-DERIVED 2026-09-02, 19.0 -> 4.35, AND THE ROW STOPS BEING `assumed`. Pre-registered in validation/renin_gain_prereg.md, written before any source was opened and sitting before this change in history; verify with git log --diff-filter=A on that file. Reproduce with python validation/renin_gain_extract.py. Branch R1. || THE DERIVATION, and it is one line. Raas.jl sets pra -> 1 + g_renin*(P_thr - MAP)/MAP_ref, so d(pra)/d(MAP) = -g_renin/MAP_ref, and pra is normalised to the plateau. van Ochten reports the same derivative as 0.05 of plateau renin per mmHg. Therefore g_renin = 0.05 * MAP_ref = 0.05 * 87.0 = 4.35. || THE PREVIOUS NOTE ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT THE SOURCE, AND THAT IS WHY THE ROW SAT `assumed` FOR SIX DAYS. It said van Ochten 'reports the renal baroreflex slope in animal units this model cannot consume directly, so the gain is fitted rather than converted.' The paper says the opposite in its own Limitations: it could NOT meta-analyse absolute renin because studies reported PRA, PRC or renin release on assay-dependent scales, so it converted the dose-response to PERCENTAGE OF BASELINE - which is the one form this model can consume, because pra here is dimensionless and normalised. The units were never the obstacle. Nobody had opened the paper. || ONE SIGNIFICANT FIGURE IN THE SOURCE, THREE IN THE VALUE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ARITHMETIC NOT PRECISION. '50 percentage points per 10 mmHg' carries one figure. 4.35 is stored so that g_renin = 0.05*MAP_ref reproduces exactly and stays exact if CV.MAP.SETPOINT moves again; the third digit is the conversion, not a measurement. Directive 1.9. A test asserts the identity rather than the digits. || SPECIES AND TIER. Animal, mixed (rat, dog, mouse, rabbit, cat, fowl). ADR 0006 E2 under an ethical ceiling: servo-controlling renal perfusion pressure is not performable in humans, the same clause RAAS.RENIN.PRESSURE_THRESHOLD already invokes from this same paper. TIER B RATHER THAN THE THRESHOLD ROW'S A, deliberately: the threshold 93 +/- 2 comes from the full 30-study dose-response meta-analysis, while this slope is quoted only for the 5-comparison healthy-versus-hypertensive subset (Figure 6). The paper gives no numeric slope for the 30-study analysis in text - Figure 4 would have to be digitised, which is a different extraction_method. The paper also states 'Risk of bias was high in most studies.' || VALIDITY RANGE. The linear regression was fitted below 90 mmHg renal arterial pressure; the plateau was averaged above 105; the threshold is their intersection. This model runs at MAP 82-87, INSIDE the fitted linear range, so no extrapolation is involved. The pre-existing simplification that systemic MAP is used directly as renal perfusion pressure is unchanged by this row and is Raas.jl's, not this row's. || WHAT IT CHANGES, MEASURED with bench/renin_gain_sweep.jl. Resting pra falls 2.31 -> 1.30 relative to the plateau. THE SALT-STEP STEADY STATE DOES NOT MOVE: escape drives fr_mod to zero, and a 16-fold change in this gain moves the shift by at most 0.81%, so the headline 5.0570 mmHg is unchanged to five significant figures. THE STEADY STATE WITH ESCAPE SUPPRESSED DOES MOVE, and that is ADR 0015's configuration: the fall in the salt-step shift goes from 50.7% at 19.0 to about 22% here. ADR 0015 stays LIVE by its own pre-registered 20% rule and its magnitude more than halves. || DECLARED STRUCTURAL LIMITATION, branch S2 of the pre-registration, and it is NOT a defect in this value. The rectified linear form caps the PRA ratio it can produce between two pressures at the ratio of their drives, independently of the gain. van den Bosch 2021 (PMID 34921521, n = 70 healthy men) reports PRA 2.10 on high salt against 5.74 on low, a ratio of 2.73, at MAP 88 against 86 - where this form's ceiling is (93-86)/(93-88) = 1.40. NO VALUE OF THIS GAIN REPRODUCES THAT. Human salt-induced renin runs mostly through macula densa sodium delivery and renal sympathetic traffic, neither of which this component has. The pre-registration forbade fitting to those data for exactly this reason, and the gap is recorded in HANDOVER section 7 rather than absorbed into this number - which is how RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE became a hypertensive value (section 3.3).

name: Additive fractional sodium reabsorption per unit aldosterone
notes: ASSUMED, not measured and NOT fitted to any published target. Recorded as assumed rather than calibrated because the target itself is an assumption: no source gives this quantity in a form the model can consume, so there was nothing to calibrate against. Sized so the peak unescaped tubular effect is about half a percent of filtered load, the order of magnitude implied by the 27% acute fall in urinary sodium excretion reported by Kelly and Nelson. NOT derived from it - converting a urinary excretion change into a fractional reabsorption increment needs the filtered load at the time, which that paper does not report. Same standing as RAAS.RENIN.PRESSURE_GAIN: escape zeroes fr_mod at steady state so this shapes the transient only.

name: Osmotic threshold for vasopressin release
citation: Zerbe RL, Miller JZ, Robertson GL. The reproducibility and heritability of individual differences in osmoregulatory function in normal human subjects. J Lab Clin Med 1991;117(1):51-59.
notes: Linear regression of plasma vasopressin on plasma osmolality during hypertonic saline infusion. Individual thresholds ranged 280 to 288 mOsm/kg and the frequency distribution across 80 healthy adults was essentially normal, so the MIDPOINT 284.0 is adopted and the range is carried as the uncertainty rather than an SD, which the paper does not give in a poolable form. Thresholds correlated within monozygotic but not dizygotic twins. NOTE the companion SENSITIVITY spans 0.12 to 1.66 pg/ml per mOsm/kg - fourteen-fold, and highly reproducible within a subject at r = 0.94 - which is NOT used here because this model carries no plasma vasopressin concentration. That spread is the obvious population covariate for src/ensemble.jl. Verified against PMID 1987308 on 2026-08-25.

name: Minimum urine osmolality at full water diuresis
notes: ASSUMED and NOT SOURCED. A relationship-shaped search for maximal and minimal urinary concentrating ability in healthy humans returned lithium cohorts, hydration indices and clinical case series - none characterising the limit in a healthy population in a form this model can consume. 50 mOsm/kg is the conventional figure and it is recorded as an assumption rather than dressed in a textbook citation nobody opened. IT SETS THE MAXIMAL DIURESIS: with the assumed solute load it gives 12.0 L/day, which is plausible but unverified. Source this before using the component near the dilute end.

name: Maximum urine osmolality at maximal antidiuresis
citation: Tryding N, Berg B, Ekman S, Nilsson JE, Sterner G, Harris A. DDAVP test for renal concentration capacity. Age-related reference intervals. Scand J Urol Nephrol 1988;22(2):141-145.
notes: SOURCED 2026-09-01, AND THE TEXTBOOK 1200 WAS HIGH. Was 1200.0 mOsm/kg, DERIVED as RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD / RN.H2O.OBLIGATORY_LOSS = 600 / 0.5 - maximal concentrating ability computed from an obligatory volume that was itself `assumed` with an empty citation. The dependency was backwards: MAXIMAL CONCENTRATING ABILITY IS WHAT IS MEASURED, by water deprivation or DDAVP, and the obligatory volume is what follows from it given a solute load. RN.H2O.OBLIGATORY_LOSS is now derived from this row. Pre-re-registered in validation/dependency_inversion_prereg.md, which was committed BEFORE any paper was opened and sits immediately before this change in main's history. NO COMMIT SHA IS CITED, DELIBERATELY - rebase-merge rewrites it and every such citation already in this ledger points at a commit main does not contain. Verify the ordering instead: git log --diff-filter=A -- validation/dependency_inversion_prereg.md. NOW REPORTED: Tryding 1988. Maximal urinary concentration after a single 4 microgram subcutaneous injection of DDAVP in 212 healthy adults aged 20 to 80. Mean values decline significantly with age, 982 mOsm/kg at 20 years to 823 at 80. 982 IS THE VALUE AT THE YOUNG ADULT END and is adopted because U_max is a CEILING - the saturation limit of the ADH curve in Adh.jl, reached at adh = 1 - rather than a population mean. The age decline is real, is roughly 16% across six decades, and this model has no age dimension: recorded as debt, not approximated. The same paper reports that maximal osmolality did not differ significantly between strict fluid restriction and liberal intake before the DDAVP, so the number is not an artefact of the deprivation protocol. CORROBORATED, NOT POOLED. Bech AP, Wetzels JFM, Nijenhuis T. Reference values of renal tubular function tests are dependent on age and kidney function. Physiol Rep 2017;5(23):e13542. Median maximal urine osmolality after desmopressin 1002 mOsm/kg in healthy individuals aged 18-50, 820 in healthy individuals over 50, 624 with compromised renal function. Two independent studies thirty years apart, both near 1000 in young healthy adults and both near 820 in the old. NOT POOLED: Bech reports a MEDIAN of 10 subjects and Tryding a fitted mean by age, and pooling.md forbids inventing a rule that fits them. SINGLE SOURCE, k = 1, rule 6. WHAT WAS SCREENED AND NOT USED. Fourteen further queries over two sweeps returned paediatric series, lithium and polycystic-kidney cohorts, desmopressin bioequivalence studies and hydration-marker papers. Nadvornikova 1980 (Clin Nephrol 1980;14(3):142-147, 45 healthy volunteers, standardised DDAVP protocol) is the right design but reports no normative osmolality in the record read. Curtis 1979 (Br Med J 1979;1(6159):304-305) reports that most normal subjects reach maximal concentration spontaneously over 24 hours, which supports the protocol but gives no value. NO DISPERSION IS ENTERED. Tryding reports age-related reference INTERVALS; the record read gives the age-related means, not an SD at a given age. Directive 1.12 wants a centre with spread and this row has only the centre - recorded rather than invented.

name: Normalised antidiuretic activity per mOsm/kg above threshold
citation: Derived to close baseline water balance; see notes.
notes: PRECISION: rounded to 3 significant figures on 2026-08-27. The sources do not support more, and carrying digits that do not exist forced the closure gate and the test suite to chase arithmetic noise. Derived rows inherit the significant figures of their inputs and are rounded to match; the closure tolerance was moved to 1e-3 in the same change, which is still an order of magnitude tighter than the 6% error that motivated that gate. || DERIVED, not fitted and not assumed. Forced by requiring that at the plasma osmolality setpoint the model excretes exactly intake minus insensible loss, which is what the pre-ADH placeholder did. k_adh = ((solute/(intake-insensible)) - U_min) / ((U_max - U_min) * (Osm_set - Osm_thr)) = 0.08780904 per mOsm/kg, giving antidiuretic activity 0.263427 at baseline - a quarter of maximal, with room to move both ways. Closure constraint enforced by tools/check_closure.py. THIS IS NOT ZERBE'S SENSITIVITY: that is 0.12-1.66 pg/ml per mOsm/kg and this is a normalised 0-1 activity, because no sourced map from plasma vasopressin to urine osmolality was found. || RECOMPUTED 2026-09-01, 0.0878 -> 0.10835, when ADH.URINE.OSM_MAX moved 1200 -> 982 (Tryding 1988). k_adh = ((solute/v_base) - U_min) / ((U_max - U_min) * (Osm_set - Osm_thr)) = (352.941176 - 50) / (932 * 3). The DERIVATION is unchanged and so is the operating point it pins: at the plasma osmolality setpoint the model still excretes exactly intake minus insensible loss, by construction. What changes is the SLOPE - a lower ceiling reached over the same osmolality span means each mOsm/kg buys more antidiuretic activity. Five significant figures because the closure check compares this against its own derivation at 1e-3 relative and three figures would fail it.

citation: Derived from RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD, BF.H2O.INTAKE_NOMINAL and BF.H2O.INSENSIBLE_LOSS.
notes: PRECISION: rounded to 3 significant figures on 2026-08-27. The sources do not support more, and carrying digits that do not exist forced the closure gate and the test suite to chase arithmetic noise. Derived rows inherit the significant figures of their inputs and are rounded to match; the closure tolerance was moved to 1e-3 in the same change, which is still an order of magnitude tighter than the 6% error that motivated that gate. || DERIVED: solute load / (intake - insensible loss) = 600 / 1.7 = 352.941176. Used ONLY by the disabled branch, where it holds urine osmolality at the value that reproduces the old placeholder water excretion exactly, so enabled=false recovers pre-ADH behaviour. name: Daily urinary solute excretion
notes: ASSUMED and NOT SOURCED, and it is the load-bearing assumption of the ADH component - urine volume is this divided by urine osmolality, so it scales the whole water-excretion limb. 600 mOsm/day is a conventional adult figure. It is HELD CONSTANT, which is itself a modelling choice: in reality it tracks protein and salt intake, so a salt step should move it and here it does not. That omission makes the model under-respond to a salt load on the water side. Source it, and consider making it depend on Na_excr, before trusting any water result under a changed diet.

name: Urinary osmoles per mEq of sodium excreted
citation: Imamura T, Kinugawa K, Minatsuki S, Muraoka H, Kato N, Inaba T, Maki H, Shiga T, Hatano M, Yao A, Kyo S, Komuro I. Urine osmolality estimated using urine urea nitrogen, sodium and creatinine can effectively predict response to tolvaptan in decompensated heart failure patients. Circ J 2013;77(5):1208-1213. PMID 23318562. The validated estimator carries urine sodium with a coefficient of 2.
notes: THE COEFFICIENT IS ELECTRONEUTRALITY, NOT A FITTED CONSTANT. Every sodium ion leaving in the urine leaves with an accompanying anion, predominantly chloride, so one mEq of excreted sodium contributes approximately two milliosmoles - one for the cation and one for the anion. That is why the standard urine osmolality estimators all carry urine sodium with a coefficient of 2. WHAT THE CITATION ACTUALLY SUPPLIES. Imamura 2013 validated the whole estimator 1.07*(2*[urine Na] + [urine urea nitrogen]/2.8 + [urine creatinine]*2/3) + 16 against MEASURED urine osmolality in 66 patients and reports r = 0.938, p < 0.001. The paper does not measure this coefficient; it measures that a formula containing it reproduces the real thing. That is the honest description of the evidence and is why this row is tier B rather than A. DECLARED LIMITATION OF THE COHORT: decompensated heart failure patients receiving tolvaptan, i.e. a diseased population under a V2 antagonist. Directive 1.7 test - had the correlation come out poorly, the conclusion would have been that estimated urine osmolality cannot predict tolvaptan response, so the composition relation is the INSTRUMENT there and not the subject. It is accepted anyway because the coefficient is not an empirical finding of that paper but a charge-balance requirement, and the validation is corroboration that the requirement holds in real urine. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE STRUCTURE, not pooled with it: Alwis US, Delanghe J, Dossche L, Walle JV, Van Camp J, Monaghan TF, Roggeman S, Everaert K. Could evening dietary protein intake play a role in nocturnal polyuria? J Clin Med 2020;9(8):2532. name: Non-sodium urinary solute load, held constant
citation: Derived from RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD, RN.URINE.OSM_PER_NA and BF.NA.INTAKE_MID.
notes: DERIVED, and it is a RESIDUAL rather than a measurement: SOLUTE_NONNA = RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD - RN.URINE.OSM_PER_NA * BF.NA.INTAKE_MID = 600.0 - 2.0 * 154.0 = 292.0 mOsm/day. It stands for urea plus potassium salts plus everything else, all held constant. WHY IT IS DEFINED THIS WAY. RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD is load-bearing: ADH.URINE.OSM_MAX, ADH.URINE.OSM_BASELINE and ADH.OSM.SENSITIVITY are all derived from it and four closure checks depend on it. Making the solute load track sodium must therefore leave the REFERENCE load untouched, or every derived ADH constant and every steady state moves. Pinning the residual so that total load returns exactly 600.0 at the mid salt arm (154 mEq/day) achieves that: the mid arm is unchanged to the last digit and only the high and low arms move. INHERITED DEBT, STATED PLAINLY: 292 mOsm/day is almost certainly TOO LOW for the non-sodium fraction. Urea alone is normally the largest single contributor to urine osmolality (Alwis 2020) and potassium salts add roughly another 100-120 mOsm/day, so a real non-sodium remainder on a Western diet is nearer 400-500. The residual is small because the parent RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD = 600 mOsm/day is itself an unsourced conventional figure that is low for a 154 mEq/day sodium intake - typical measured totals are 700-900. THIS ROW DOES NOT FIX THAT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS FIXING IT. Correcting the total would move U_max, U_base, k_adh and every steady state, and needs its own pre-registered extraction. What this row does is make the load RESPOND to salt, which it previously did not do at all. Tier C, inherited from the parent.

citation: Petersen SE, Aung N, Sanghvi MM, Zemrak F, Fung K, Paiva JM, Francis JM, Khanji MY, Lukaschuk E, Lee AM, Carapella V, Kim YJ, Leeson P, Piechnik SK, Neubauer S. notes: SOURCED 2026-09-01, AND THE DEPENDENCY NOW RUNS THE WAY THE MEASUREMENT DOES. NO COMMIT SHA IS CITED, DELIBERATELY - rebase-merge rewrites it and every such citation already in this ledger points at a commit main does not contain. Verify the ordering instead: git log --diff-filter=A -- validation/dependency_inversion_prereg.md. HANDOVER section 4 item 1. NOW REPORTED: Petersen 2017, UK Biobank CMR. Left ventricular stroke volume 96 +/- 20 mL in 368 men. Cohort: 804 participants remaining after exclusion for non-Caucasian ethnicity, known cardiovascular disease and any condition affecting chamber size or function, of whom 800 (368 men, 432 women) have ventricular measurements. Ages 45-74. SINGLE SOURCE, k = 1, pooling.md rule 6 - stated plainly and not dressed as consensus. TECHNIQUE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance, steady-state free precession at 1.5 T, manual contouring, PAPILLARY MUSCLES AND TRABECULATIONS INCLUDED IN THE LV VOLUME. Zhan 2024 (Circ Cardiovasc Imaging 2024;17(2):e016090, 254 studies screened, 12,812 healthy adults) exists because that convention moves LV volumes, and it pools the two conventions SEPARATELY rather than across them. pooling.md prohibits pooling across incompatible measurement methods, so this row is single-source BY RULE and not by neglect. WHAT WAS SCREENED AND WHY IT WAS NOT USED, so the next attempt does not repeat it. (1) Zhan 2024, the meta-analysis pooling.md rule 1 would have preferred: reports lower and upper reference LIMITS, indexed to body surface area. range-midpoint is prohibited for new entries and the model carries no BSA, so it fails twice. (2) Luu 2022, Canadian Alliance for Healthy Hearts and Minds (J Cardiovasc Magn Reson 2022;24(1):2), n = 3206, multi-ethnic, anatomically correct contouring - LARGER AND BETTER DESIGNED THAN THE ROW ADOPTED, and reports LVSV INDEXED ONLY (46 +/- 8 male, 42 +/- 7 female mL/m2). Converting it needs a BSA formula, which this model does not carry and which the pre-registration explicitly refused to introduce as a side effect. It also contours papillary muscles into LV MASS rather than volume, so it could not be pooled with Petersen in any case. (3) Patel 2021 WASE (PMID 34044105) paywalled, no numbers in the abstract - recorded against CV.CO.NOMINAL since 2026-08-31 and still unopened. (5) Salton 2002 Framingham Offspring (n = 142) and Le Ven 2016 (n = 434, mean age 26) - both report the direction but not absolute stroke volume in the record read. NOT NORMALISED TO THE REFERENCE MASS, AND THAT IS RECORDED DEBT RATHER THAN A CHOICE. This value is EXTENSIVE and is multiplied by size_factor = body_mass / BF.BODY_MASS.REFERENCE, so it should be stated at 70 kg. Petersen reports body weight by AGE GROUP (71, 71, 69 kg) but NOT by sex, so the cohort mean is essentially the reference mass while the male and female subgroups plainly are not. The pre-registration fixed the rule in advance: normalise where cohort mass is reported by sex, otherwise enter as reported and record the mismatch. So this pair still carries a body-size component, and in the ensemble - where mass is sampled by sex - that component is counted twice. Fixing it needs sex-stratified cohort mass or a BSA row. AND THE PREDICTION FIXED IN ADVANCE WAS HALF WRONG, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. The previous note on this row cited Katori 1979 for NO significant sex difference in stroke INDEX and concluded the dimorphism is body size, not the heart. Petersen indexes to BSA and the difference SURVIVES: 49 +/- 10 male against 45 +/- 8 female mL/m2, a 9% male excess where the absolute difference is 28%. Luu 2022 finds the same on 3206 people (46 vs 42), Salton 2002 states volumetric measures remain greater in men after BSA adjustment, and Le Ven 2016 states all gender differences remained after normalisation. Four independent cohorts. So body size carries roughly two thirds of the difference and about a third is not size - the pair was expected to collapse the way ECF per kg did when blood volume and haematocrit were sourced, and it does not.

name: Central pulse pressure, nominal
citation: Derived from CV.SBP.CENTRAL_NOMINAL and CV.DBP.CENTRAL_NOMINAL.
notes: DERIVED: PP = SBP - DBP = 109 - 76 = 33 mmHg, which reproduces the central pulse pressure of 33 mmHg the paper reports independently. That agreement is a check on the extraction, not a coincidence. Closure constraint.

name: Fraction of pulse pressure lying BELOW mean pressure
notes: ASSUMED at the conventional one third, which is the familiar MAP = DBP + PP/3. Discharges the TODO in reconstruct.jl, which carried this as a HARDCODED default of 0.4 and demanded a ledger row before the function was used for anything - directive 1.4 is now satisfied. NAME AND JUSTIFICATION CORRECTED 2026-08-27; THE VALUE IS UNCHANGED AND WAS ALWAYS RIGHT. This row was entered as 'Fraction of pulse pressure lying ABOVE mean pressure', and 0.3333 is the fraction lying BELOW it. Against the tier A central pressures in this same ledger - SBP 109, DBP 76, PP 33, MAP 87 - the fraction above the mean is (109-87)/33 = 0.667 and the fraction below is (87-76)/33 = 0.333. The old note's reasoning was inverted in the same way: it said 'the fraction of pulse pressure above mean must be below 0.5 because diastole is longer than systole', and diastole being longer is exactly why MAP sits NEARER DIASTOLIC, which makes the fraction BELOW the mean the one that must be under 0.5. The 0.515 that exposed the brachial/central mixing was (93-76)/33, a below-mean fraction, so the impossibility argument itself was correct and only its label was wrong. WHY IT MATTERED. check_closure.py uses this row as MAP = DBP + k*PP, i.e. with the CORRECT below-mean meaning, and passes. reconstruct.jl defined its form_factor as the fraction ABOVE the mean and computed SBP = MAP + form_factor*PP. Wiring the ledger row into that function under the shared name 'form factor' would have produced SBP 98.0 and DBP 65.0 against the sourced 109 and 76 - both wrong by PP/3 = 11 mmHg, in opposite directions - and NO GATE WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, because the closure check never reaches reconstruct.jl. Found while connecting that file, not by any check. reconstruct.jl now takes k_below explicitly and names the convention in its signature. NOT CONSTANT IN REALITY, and reconstruct.jl calls treating it as constant the single largest error source in the reconstruction: it varies with heart rate, arterial stiffness, disease state, and - as the 87 versus 89.8 discrepancy shows - with measurement site. Source it before any claim about pulse pressure as an endpoint.

name: Total arterial compliance
citation: Derived from CV.SV.NOMINAL and CV.PP.CENTRAL_NOMINAL; form validated by Chemla 1998.
notes: RECOMPUTED 2026-09-01 when CV.SV.NOMINAL was sourced. C_art = SV0 / PP0 = 96 / 33.0 = 2.909 mL/mmHg. Was 2.445. It cannot disagree at the operating point. The Chemla 1998 SV/PP estimator is defined on AORTIC pressure, which is why PP here is the central value. name: Fractional ECF volume half-span over which the GFR volume response is evidenced
citation: van den Bosch JJJON, Hessels NR, Visser FW, Krikken JA, Bakker SJL, Riphagen IJ, Navis GJ. Plasma sodium, extracellular fluid volume, and blood pressure in healthy men. Physiol Rep 2021;9(24):e15103. doi:10.14814/phy2.15103. PMID 34921521. PMC8683787. n = 70 healthy normotensive men, crossover, 7 days per level, intake verified by 24 h urinary sodium (230 +/- 67 against 38 +/- 26 mmol/24 h). Table 1: ECFV 17.4 +/- 1.66 against 16.5 +/- 1.54 L/1.73 m2 by 125I-iothalamate, BSA 2.04 +/- 0.15 against 2.03 +/- 0.15. THE HALF-SPAN OF THE TESTED EXTRACELLULAR VOLUME RANGE, derived from those four numbers; the paper does not report it as a range. The derivation is validation/renal_hemodynamics_extract.py.
notes: THE CENSORING BOUND ON RN.GFR.VOLUME_SENSITIVITY, and it exists because a linear response has no support outside the volumes anyone measured. validation/renal_hemodynamics_prereg.md section 6 fixed this in advance: 'the functional form in this model is sourced only as a straight line between two measured intake levels, which is E2 inside the tested range and NOTHING AT ALL outside it, so the term is clamped to the pooled tested intake range, and that censoring is recorded on the row exactly as RN.AUTOREG.UPPER records its own.' This is that row. || THE DERIVATION. De-index each arm with its OWN body surface area, which is the correction HANDOVER section 3.12 records owing to ecf_salt_response_extract.py: high 17.4*2.04/1.73 = 20.518 L, low 16.5*2.03/1.73 = 19.361 L, mean 19.940, difference 1.157. The HALF-span about the mean is 0.5783/19.940 = 0.02900 -> 0.029. Two significant figures, per directive 1.9 and for the same reason RN.GFR.VOLUME_SENSITIVITY keeps two: the information is in a difference of two three-figure means and there is no third figure to keep. || IT IS A HALF-SPAN AND NOT A SPAN. The clamp is two-sided about the reference volume, so the bound is the distance from the mean to either arm, not the distance between the arms. Entering the span would double the evidenced range silently. || WHAT IT CENSORS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The model's chronic salt step of 103-205 mEq/day moves ECF volume about 2.4 percent either side of reference, so this bound does NOT bind on the chronic protocol - it is inert there, which is the correct outcome for a range that brackets the tested one. It DOES bind on the acute challenges: 2 L of saline expands ECF by roughly 9 percent, three times the evidenced half-span, and without the clamp the model would extrapolate a chronic 7-day relationship into a region no source reaches. || THE TIMESCALE EXTRAPOLATION IS SEPARATE AND IS DECLARED, NOT BOUNDED BY THIS ROW. The source is chronic, 7 days per level, and the model applies the response algebraically and therefore instantly. Conlin 1993 (PMID 7503952) shows the renal response to volume expansion per se within 3-7 hours, by saline or dextran alike, so an instantaneous term is fast rather than backwards - but nothing here sources a time constant, and a lag was deliberately NOT added because its tau would be identified by nothing, which is the defect RN.ANP.TAU already carries. || SPECIES human and the cohort is MEN, inheriting the sex conflict recorded in full on RN.GFR.VOLUME_SENSITIVITY: Pechere-Bertschi 2002 finds no change in renal haemodynamics on high salt in the follicular phase in 35 normotensive women. If that row becomes a sexed pair this bound must be re-derived with it.

name: Ventilatory sensitivity to CO2 above the recruitment threshold

citation: Derived. See notes.
notes: Haemoglobin binds four O2 per tetramer, so the capacity is four molar volumes per molecular weight: 4 x 22414 mL/mol / 64458 g/mol = 1.3909 -> 1.391 mL/g. || THE 1.34 AGAINST 1.39 QUESTION, SETTLED IN THE OPEN BECAUSE validation/blood_gas_prereg.md SECTION 3 REQUIRED IT. name: Severinghaus dissociation coefficient A
citation: Severinghaus JW. Simple, accurate equations for human blood O2 dissociation computations. J Appl Physiol Respir Environ Exerc Physiol 1979;46(3):599-602. doi:10.1152/jappl.1979.46.3.599. PMID 35496. ABSTRACT READ - the equation and its stated accuracy are both in the abstract, which is the part used. The paper fits the STANDARD HUMAN BLOOD O2 dissociation curve to within +/- 0.0055 fractional saturation over 0 < S < 1.
notes: ONE OF TWO COEFFICIENTS OF A SINGLE PUBLISHED FIT. S = 1/(A/(PO2^3 + B*PO2) + 1). THEY ARE NOT SEPARATELY MEASURABLE AND MUST MOVE TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL - neither has a physical meaning on its own, and changing one without the other produces a curve nobody published. || BRANCH B3 OF validation/blood_gas_prereg.md, AND THE PRE-REGISTRATION PREFERRED OTHERWISE. Section 4 preferred the Hill form because its two parameters - P50 and the exponent - are separately measurable and would get separate rows with separate provenance. THE DECOMPOSITION FAILED: searching for a measured P50 and Hill exponent in healthy humans returns chronic obstructive lung disease, sickle cell disease, chronic hypoxaemia, sleep apnoea and congenital heart disease, every one excluded by section 2, several of them existing to characterise a pulse oximeter rather than the physiology (directive 1.7). So a published fit is taken whole, with its citation and its stated error, and the loss of decomposability is the recorded cost. || A PUBLISHED EQUATION FITTED TO MEASURED DATA IS NOT ANOTHER MODEL'S OUTPUT, which is the distinction validation/targets.md draws and the reason this is admissible at all. || THE IMPLIED P50 IS 26.86 Torr, SOLVED FROM THE EQUATION AND DELIBERATELY NOT A LEDGER ROW, so it cannot silently disagree with the curve it comes from. check_closure.py asserts it lands in the human range, which makes it a TEST of the adopted equation rather than a second definition of the same quantity. Severinghaus's own Bohr equation uses PO2/26.6 as its reference, so 26.86 is consistent with the paper to within 1 percent. || FIXED AT NORMAL pH AND TEMPERATURE. ADR 0018 records what that disqualifies: the Bohr effect, fever and hypothermia, 2,3-DPG, and the increased offloading in exercising muscle. pH needs bicarbonate, which is renal and absent. || INTENSIVE.

name: Alveolar-arterial oxygen difference, young adult
citation: NOT SOURCED. The correct source was identified and could not be opened: Crapo RO, Jensen RL, Hegewald M, Tashkin DP. Arterial blood gas reference values for sea level and an altitude of 1,400 meters. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 1999;160(5 Pt 1):1525-31. doi:10.1164/ajrccm.160.5.9806006. PMID 10556115. It is the least precisely known stage of the chain and it sits directly upstream of arterial saturation, which is the output ADR 0018's first falsifiable test judges. || IT WAS NOT TUNED, AND THAT IS DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. name: Fall in log-e thyrotropin per unit free thyroxine
citation: Benhadi N, Fliers E, Visser TJ, Reitsma JB, Wiersinga WM. Pilot study on the assessment of the setpoint of the hypothalamus-pituitary-thyroid axis in healthy volunteers. Eur J Endocrinol 2010;162(2):323-9. doi:10.1530/EJE-09-0655. PMID 19926783. ABSTRACT ONLY - the publisher origin returns a Cloudflare 525 and the Erasmus repository record Unpaywall points at holds metadata but no file. n = 21 healthy volunteers, 9 male 12 female, mean age 60 (range 51-74), randomised to placebo / 125 / 250 ug T4 or placebo / 25 / 50 ug T3 at two-week intervals. AN INTERVENTION, NOT A CROSS-SECTION, which is the design a feedback gain needs. Reported: log TSH = 1.50 - 0.059 x FT4, P < 0.05, whole group. || THE BASE OF THAT LOGARITHM IS NOT STATED AND IT MATTERS BY A FACTOR OF 2.30. It is resolved, NOT by which reading puts the euthyroid point in range, by a second independent measurement: Jostel A, Ryder WDJ, Shalet SM. The use of thyroid function tests in the diagnosis of hypopituitarism: definition and evaluation of the TSH Index. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf) 2009;71(4):529-34. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2265.2009.03534.x. PMID 19226261. ABSTRACT ONLY, not open access. 9519 thyroid function tests in 4064 patients, Bayer Immuno-1: 'Feedback inhibition was estimated to cause a 0.1345 decrease in log TSH (mU/l) for 1 pmol/l increase in fT4 concentration'. || Jostel's abstract also says 'log', but the index it defines is in wide clinical use and the downstream literature writes the base out: Wang Y et al. Sensitivity to Thyroid Hormones and Risk of Prediabetes. Front Endocrinol (Lausanne) 2021;12:657114. PMC8129566, OPEN ACCESS, READ IN FULL - 'TSHI = ln TSH (mIU/L) + 0.1345 * FT4 (pmol/L)'. Its own Table 1 confirms the arithmetic on n = 4378: ln(1.64) + 0.1345*13.33 = 2.29 against a reported TSHI of 2.25, where the log10 reading gives 2.01.
notes: THE FEEDBACK GAIN OF THE HUMAN THYROID AXIS, in natural-log units per pmol/L of free thyroxine. Benhadi's 0.059 read as base 10 is 0.059*ln(10) = 0.13585; Jostel's is 0.1345. THE TWO AGREE TO 1% AND ONLY UNDER THAT PAIRING - read Benhadi as ln and the two competent measurements of the same gain differ 2.3-fold, in cohorts of comparable FT4 range, which is not credible. || THE VALUE ENTERED IS BENHADI'S because that cohort is admissible under thyroid_prereg.md section 2 on every criterion and the design is an intervention; Jostel's population is a hypopituitary referral series and its purpose was to define a diagnostic index, which is directive 1.7's flag. It is the corroboration, not the value. NOT POOLED - different assays, and pooling.md forbids pooling across incompatible methods. The uncertainty range is the two estimates, not a confidence interval. || THIS ROW DISCHARGES BRANCH T3, which an earlier extraction pass took correctly on the evidence then available. || VALUE CHANGED 2026-09-05, AND THE CHANGE IS THE POINT. This row first entered Benhadi's 0.13585 alone and called Jostel's 0.1345 'corroboration, not the value', on the grounds that pooling.md forbids pooling across assays. THE TWO NUMBERS DIFFER BY 1%. Choosing between measurements that agree to within a fifth of any plausible experimental error is not rigour, it is a coin toss dressed as a decision - directive 1.9 and HANDOVER section 3.23, both of which this repository already had. The entered value is now the MEAN of the two, 0.1352, and the uncertainty is their spread. || UNWEIGHTED, because neither source reports a standard error and the weights cannot change a 1% interval by anything that matters. Method: two estimates, arithmetic mean; extraction_method is therefore derived rather than reported, since no paper prints 0.1352. || WHAT THE SPREAD IS WORTH, and it is the useful consequence: carrying both ends through the loop moves the predicted euthyroid thyrotropin from 3.32 to 3.39 mIU/L, about 2%. So the slope is NOT where the model's 2.4x thyrotropin discrepancy comes from, and that is now arithmetic rather than assertion.

name: Log-e thyrotropin extrapolated to zero free thyroxine
citation: Benhadi N, Fliers E, Visser TJ, Reitsma JB, Wiersinga WM. Pilot study on the assessment of the setpoint of the hypothalamus-pituitary-thyroid axis in healthy volunteers. Eur J Endocrinol 2010;162(2):323-9. doi:10.1530/EJE-09-0655. PMID 19926783. ABSTRACT ONLY - the publisher origin returns a Cloudflare 525 and the Erasmus repository record Unpaywall points at holds metadata but no file. n = 21 healthy volunteers, 9 male 12 female, mean age 60 (range 51-74), randomised to placebo / 125 / 250 ug T4 or placebo / 25 / 50 ug T3 at two-week intervals. AN INTERVENTION, NOT A CROSS-SECTION, which is the design a feedback gain needs. Reported: log TSH = 1.50 - 0.059 x FT4, P < 0.05, whole group. || Intercept 1.50 in base-10 units, so 1.50*ln(10) = 3.453878. The base is fixed by the same argument as THY.TSH.FT4_SLOPE.
notes: THE LOAD-BEARING WEAKNESS OF THIS AXIS, AND IT IS SAID HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. The slope has two independent estimates agreeing to 1% and the euthyroid FT4 has two agreeing to within a standard deviation; THIS NUMBER HAS ONE SOURCE AND IT CARRIES THE WHOLE OF THE MODEL'S DISCREPANCY IN THYROTROPIN. Reconstructing it from independent euthyroid pairs at the agreed slope gives 2.72 (Maushart euthyroid visit), 2.82 (Maushart 3-month) and 2.59 (NHANES III geometric mean TSH at the sourced FT4) - all 0.6 to 0.9 log units below 3.454, a factor of 1.9-2.4 in TSH. || WHY IT WOULD BE HIGH, AND THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME PATTERN IN THIS REPOSITORY: an intercept is a line extrapolated to FT4 = 0 from data that never approached zero. The same extrapolation forced the ADR 0017 amendment - a chemoreflex line extrapolated below its measured range put ventilation at 19.3 L/min against a real 6.2 - and produced HANDOVER section 3.22's censoring bound. Benhadi's cohort is also mean age 60 and NHANES III reports TSH rising with age. || IT IS NOT REPLACED BY ANY OF THE RECONSTRUCTIONS. Every one of them is built from a measured euthyroid TSH, which is the quantity ADR 0019's falsifiable test 2 judges the loop against; fitting to it would be HANDOVER section 3.15's error committed deliberately. The model reports a euthyroid TSH 2.4x the NHANES III geometric mean and nothing downstream consumes TSH. || CUT FROM 3.453878 TO 3.454 ON 2026-09-05. Seven significant figures on a number whose source reports three ('1.50') is exactly the false precision directive 1.9 exists to stop. || AND THE ARITHMETIC THAT CONVICTS THIS ROW RATHER THAN THE SLOPE: sweeping the slope across its full two-source spread moves the predicted euthyroid thyrotropin by 2%, against a discrepancy of 2.4x. Nothing about the slope's uncertainty reaches that. The intercept does, because slope and intercept in a regression over a narrow range are strongly anti-correlated and the intercept is the extrapolated one - Benhadi's free-thyroxine range is a euthyroid baseline plus a thyroxine load, and the intercept lies about 17 pmol/L outside it. THE ABSTRACT REPORTS NO STANDARD ERROR FOR IT, so its variance cannot be propagated and the honest statement is that this coefficient is not determined to better than roughly a factor of two by the study that reports it.
